info.title: Omnibus API
info.description: The REST API behind every Omnibus client. The web app, the iOS app and the MCP server all use it, and a new client can too. ## Signing in `POST /api/auth/login` opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`, `android` or `bearer` and the token comes back in the response body; send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer `. Leave `client_kind` out and the server sets a session cookie instead, which is what a browser wants. An API token (`omni_…`, from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`) works anywhere a session token does, and suits scripts. Some media, such as covers, audio parts and book files, gets loaded straight into an `` or `

get.description:
Answers without a session, so a client can probe a server address before signing in.
`time` lets a client measure its clock's offset before it stamps progress writes.

post.description:
Replaces your profile picture. The server checks the bytes are a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP
image and stores the type it finds, not the one sent.

schema.description: Describes the multipart form `POST /api/account/avatar` takes: one image part.

avatar.description:
A JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of at most 10 MiB, sent with an `image/*` content type.
SVG is refused.

400.description: The form has no `avatar` part, or the part isn't an `image/*` type, is SVG, or is larger than 10 MiB.

415.description: The bytes aren't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image.

delete.description:
Deletes your profile picture, so clients show your initials instead. Succeeds when you
have no avatar too.

post.description:
Chooses whether a book's detail page stops at each section as you scroll. Read back as
`book_detail_scroll_stops` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

Replaces the list of formats your library view leaves out. Clients pass the saved list,
read back as `hidden_formats` on `GET /api/auth/me`, as the listing's `exclude_formats`.

422.description: A format name isn't 1 to 16 letters or digits, or the list has more than 32; the body says which.

post.description:
Sets or clears the address `POST /api/kindle/send` emails books to. Read back as
`kindle_email` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

422.description: The address doesn't look like an email address, or is over 320 bytes.

post.description:
Sets or clears the name other readers see on your journal entries, ratings and shared
stats. With no display name, your username shows instead.

422.description: The name is longer than 64 characters or has a control character.

post.description:
Chooses whether other readers on this server can see your reading stats. Read back as
`share_stats` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

Chooses whether your library grid folds each series into one tile. Read back as
`stack_series` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

delete.description:
Deletes a device registration, whoever it belongs to, and signs out every session on
it. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The device's id, from the devices listing.

204.description: The device and its sessions are gone.

get.description:
One snapshot of the library index, the background task queue, the search index, disk
use and the most recent errors. Poll it to keep a view current. Needs an admin account.

post.summary: Bake metadata edits into every EPUB
post.description:
Queues a background job that writes each edited book's metadata and cover into the copy
of its EPUB that downloads serve. The library's own files aren't changed. Answers as
soon as the job is queued. Needs an admin account.

delete.description:
Signs one session out, whoever it belongs to. You can't revoke the session you sent
this request with; sign out instead. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session's id, from the sessions listing.

400.description: That is the session this request came with.

404.description: No live session has that id.

get.description:
Every account on the server, up to 1000, with its permissions and whether it is locked
out. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Makes an account with the permissions you give it, whether or not registration is open.
Needs an admin account.

409.description: That username is taken, ignoring case.

422.description: The username or password breaks a rule; the body says which.

delete.description:
Deletes the account and everything that is only theirs: progress, highlights, journal
entries, shelves and sessions. Books they added stay in the library. This can't be
undone. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The user is the last admin.

get.description:
The apps the user has signed in from, each registered as a device. An unknown user id
lists nothing. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The user's devices, most recently seen first.

post.description:
Sets a new password without asking for the old one, and signs the user out everywhere.
Needs an admin account.

204.description: The password is changed and the user's sessions are revoked.

422.description: The password breaks a rule; the body says which.

patch.description: Replaces all four permission flags. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The user is the last admin, and the change would take admin away.

get.description:
The user's live sign-ins, on browsers and apps. `is_current` is always `false` here,
even for your own session. An unknown user id lists nothing. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Ends a lockout from too many wrong passwords, so the user can sign in again now.
Succeeds when the user isn't locked too. Needs an admin account.

get.description:
One file of the audiobook as an attachment, named as it is on disk. A book made of
several parts downloads one part at a time: `part` picks which. Answers `Range`
requests, so an interrupted download can resume. Needs the download permission.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description:
One of the book's audio files, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`. Defaults to
the first.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: The part of that file to download, by its `ordinal`. Defaults to the first part.

206.description: The byte range asked for in `Range`.

304.description: The file is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

403.description: Your account lacks the download permission.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file, `file_id` isn't one of its audio files, it has no part with that ordinal, or the file is missing from disk.

416.description: The `Range` lies outside the file. `Content-Range` gives its length.

get.description:
How to play the audiobook. When every part file is a format a browser plays natively
(M4B, M4A, MP3 or AAC), `mode` is `direct`: a URL per part, each streamed with `Range`,
plus the chapters. Otherwise `mode` is `hls`, with the URL of a playlist that plays
through a server-side transcode. `file_id` picks one of a book's several audio files.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description:
One of the book's audio files, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`. Defaults to
the first.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file, `file_id` isn't one of its audio files, or the file has no parts indexed.

get.description:
One part file of an audiobook the manifest plays as `direct`, served inline for an
`<audio>` element. Use the part URLs from the manifest, which carry `file_id` when it
is needed. Answers `Range` requests, so a player can seek.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description:
The audio file the part belongs to, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`. Defaults
to the first. The manifest's part URLs already carry it.

206.description: The byte range asked for in `Range`.

304.description: The part is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file, `file_id` isn't one of its audio files, the book plays through HLS, it has no part with that ordinal, or the part is missing from disk.

416.description: The `Range` lies outside the part. `Content-Range` gives its length.

get.summary: Get your playback speed for a book
get.description: The speed you last saved for this audiobook, or `null` when you haven't saved one.

put.summary: Save your playback speed for a book
put.description: Saves the speed you play this audiobook at, from 0.5 to 3.0.

400.description: `playback_rate` isn't between 0.5 and 3.0.

get.description:
The HLS playlist for an audiobook in a format a browser can't play directly: the
manifest's `playlist_url` points here. It lists every segment the transcode makes, so
you can start playing before the transcode finishes.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file.

get.description:
One MPEG-TS segment of a transcoded audiobook, named as the playlist lists it. When the
transcode hasn't made that segment yet, the request waits for the transcode to finish.

parameters.name: segment
parameters.description: The segment's file name, such as `seg-0001.ts`.

206.description: The byte range asked for in `Range`.

304.description: The segment is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

400.description: `segment` isn't `seg-` and four digits and `.ts`.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file, or the transcode finished without that segment.

416.description: The `Range` lies outside the segment. `Content-Range` gives its length.

get.description:
How far the HLS transcode of an audiobook has got. Asking starts the transcode when it
hasn't started, so poll this while `state` is `preparing`. A failed transcode isn't
retried on its own.

404.description: No book with that uuid has an audio file.

get.description:
Names, dates and the last four characters of each live token. A token's secret is shown
only once, when it is created.

post.description:
Makes a long-lived token that authenticates as you, for scripts and integrations. Copy
`secret` from the response: the server keeps only a hash of it and can't show it again.

200.description: The new token, with its secret.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

delete.description: The token stops working at once.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

post.description:
Checks the username and password and opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`,
`android` or `bearer` to get the token in the body, for an `Authorization: Bearer`
header; without it the session arrives as a cookie. Send `device_name` as well and the
session is listed under that name.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: `device_name` or `client_version` is too long or holds control characters.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords: the account is locked for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Ends the session the request carries and clears the session cookie. Signing out of a
session that has already ended still succeeds.

get.description: The account the request's session belongs to: its permissions and preferences.

401.description: The request has no live session.

post.description:
Creates a user and signs them in, exactly as `POST /api/auth/login` does. The first
account on a new server becomes its admin. After that, registration works only while an
admin keeps it open; `GET /api/auth/registration` says whether it is.

200.description: The account exists and is signed in.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: The username or password breaks a rule; the body says which.

get.description:
Whether `POST /api/auth/register` will accept a new account. An admin opens and closes
registration with `POST /api/settings/registration`.

Every live session on your account. The one making this request has `is_current` set,
since it can't be ended from here.

delete.description:
Signs that session out wherever it is. To end the session making this request, use
`POST /api/auth/logout`.

400.description: That is the session making this request.

404.description: You have no live session with that id.

get.description:
Every author with a book in the library, surname first, each with a book count, an
accent color and whether a photo is cached. Stops at 10,000 authors.

get.summary: List your progress through each author
get.description:
For each author whose books you have opened or marked: how many you have finished, how
many you are reading, and when you last read one. Authors you haven't started are left
out.

200.description: Your progress, one row per author.

post.description:
Drops every photo found at Open Library and searches again for every author, in the
background. Uploaded photos are kept. Answers at once, before the work starts. Needs
an admin account.

get.description:
One author and all their books. `reading` holds your own status and position on each
of those books you have opened or marked. Opening an author with no photo yet starts a
search for one in the background.

The author's profile photo. When none is cached, the server looks for one at Open
Library in the background, so a later request may find it. Once Open Library has had
none, the author stays without a photo until an admin deletes the photo record or
scans again.

404.description: The author has no photo, or no author has that id.

put.description:
Sets the author's photo from an uploaded image. An uploaded photo wins over one found
at Open Library, and a scan doesn't replace it. Needs an admin account.

photo.description:
The photo: a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of 10 MiB or less, sent with an
`image/*` content type. SVG is refused.

400.description: The form has no `photo` part, or the part's content type isn't `image/*`, is SVG, or the image is larger than 10 MiB.

415.description: The bytes aren't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image.

delete.description:
Drops the author's photo, uploaded or found, and any record that Open Library had
none. The next request for the photo starts a fresh search. Succeeds when there is no
photo, and for an unknown id. Needs an admin account.

post.summary: Search Open Library for an author's photo
post.description:
Drops a photo found earlier, or the record that Open Library had none, and asks Open
Library again, answering once it has. `resolved` says whether a photo was found. An
uploaded photo is kept as it is, and the answer is `resolved: true`. Needs an admin
account.

200.description: Whether the author has a photo now.

put.summary: Set an author's photo from a URL
put.description:
Downloads the image at `url` and saves it as the author's photo, the same as an
upload: it wins over Open Library, and a scan doesn't replace it. The server fetches
the URL itself, refuses addresses inside its own network, and doesn't follow
redirects. Needs an admin account.

400.description: `url` is empty, longer than 2048 bytes, not `http` or `https`, or points inside the server's network, or what it serves isn't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of 10 MiB or less; the body says which.

post.description:
Marks a place in a book: an EPUB CFI from the reader, or seconds from the audiobook
player. Mint a `client_id` on the device and the create is safe to repeat: sending the
same `client_id` again returns the bookmark the first create made, unchanged.

400.description: `book_uuid` or `position` is blank, a field is too long, `client_id` is blank, or `client_created_at` is negative.

get.summary: List your bookmarks in a book
get.description:
Each bookmark comes placed in the book: its spine index, chapter title and how far
through the book it sits. Returns up to 1,000, and an empty list for a uuid no book has.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description:
`position` (the default) lists them in reading order through the book, with any the
server can't place last. `chronological` (or `created`) lists them oldest first. Any
other value means `position`.

put.description: Replaces the bookmark's title. A null or absent `title` removes it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bookmark's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

400.description: The title is over 512 characters.

404.description: You have no bookmark with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bookmark's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

404.description: You have no bookmark with that id.

post.description:
Folds the source book into the target: the target takes the source's files, links,
identifiers and every reader's progress, highlights and other data, and the source
book disappears. `POST /api/books/merge/undo` with the returned `merge_log_id` reverses
it. Needs an admin account.

404.description: No book has the source or target uuid; the body says which.

422.description: The source and target are the same book.

get.description:
Searches the ebook and audiobook libraries for a book to merge another into, and returns
up to 20 matches. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free text, optionally with `author:`, `series:`, `tag:` and `genre:` terms. At most
1024 bytes.

400.description: `q` is missing or over 1024 bytes.

post.description:
Splits a merged book back into the two it was made from, and returns the restored
source book's uuid. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The merge is already undone, or something changed since that undo can't settle, such as a later merge into the same book; the body says what.

get.description:
Everything needed to show how the ebook and the audiobook line up: the link and whether
it is out of date, the ebook's chapters, the audio files with their chapters, the anchor
pairs, and your current position in each format.

post.summary: Turn follow mode on or off
post.description:
With follow on, a client moves to the newer position in the other format without
asking. Needs a confirmed link.

Confirms how the ebook and the audiobook line up, which turns position sync between
them on. Confirming again replaces the link; your sync points survive only when the
audio files, their order, the mode and the primary narration are all unchanged. The
path's uuid is used, not the body's `book_uuid`. `audio_order` also reorders the book's
audio files for every user, so sending it needs the edit permission.

204.description: The formats are linked and sync is on.

403.description: The body has `audio_order` and your account lacks the edit permission.

409.description: `audio_order` doesn't list exactly the book's current audio files.

422.description: `narrations` mode came without `primary_book_file_id`, or `audio_order` repeats a file.

delete.description:
Removes the link, which turns position sync between the formats off. Succeeds whether
or not a link existed.

get.summary: Get the resume point in the other format
get.description:
For a book you have as both an ebook and an audiobook: your position in the other
format, mapped onto `target`, when it is newer than your position in `target`. Without
a candidate, `state` says why: the formats aren't linked, the link is out of date
because the audio files changed, or there is nothing newer to resume.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description:
The format you want to resume in. The position in the other format is mapped onto
it.

parameters.name: derive
parameters.description:
Set to `cfi` to also get the mapped point as an EPUB CFI in the candidate's
`epub_cfi`, when `target` is `epub`. This opens the book's EPUB, so it is slower.
Any other value is ignored.

200.description: The resume candidate, or the reason there is none.

400.description: `target` is missing, or not `epub` or `audio`.

post.summary: Delete a book's files or copies
post.description:
Deletes the listed files from disk and the listed physical copies from the collection.
When nothing of the book is left, the book goes too, with every reader's data for it:
the `impact` that `GET /api/books/{uuid}/deletion-manifest` counts. This can't be undone.
Needs an admin account.

200.description: What was deleted, and whether the book went with it.

422.description: A file or copy id isn't one of this book's; the body says which.

get.description:
What `POST /api/books/{uuid}/delete-files` can delete for this book, its files and
physical copies, and how much reader data deleting all of them would take with the
book. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The book's files and copies, and the reader data at stake.

post.description:
Says "this spot in the format I'm using matches where I am in the other one". The body
gives your position in the declaring format; your saved position in the other format
supplies the match. The pair calibrates how the formats map from then on. A book with
one audio file and no link gets linked, with follow on; an existing link keeps its
follow setting. The path's uuid is used, not the body's `book_uuid`.

409.description: The book has several audio files and no link yet, the audio files changed since the link was confirmed, or the pair can't be made: the other format has no saved position, or a position names no audio file of the link.

422.description: An `epub` declaration lacks `ebook_fraction` or has one outside 0 to 1, or an `audio` declaration lacks `audio_seconds` or has a negative one.

get.description: The full-size cover image, in the format it was stored in.

304.description: The cover is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No book has that uuid, or the book has no cover.

post.description:
The current `etag` of each file you name, so a device can learn in one request which of
its downloaded books changed: compare each with the `etag` saved at download time. A file
that is gone, or that the scanner hasn't measured yet, comes back without an `etag`. Read
that as "can't tell", never as "unchanged".

200.description: One answer per file asked about.

422.description: The request names more than 500 files.

get.description:
The library's books, ebooks and audiobooks together. Without paging parameters the
response is the whole library, capped at 50,000 books: `X-Total-Count` holds the true
total, and `X-Total-Cap` appears when the cap cut the list short. Set `sort`, `dir`,
`limit` or `cursor` to page through it instead, following `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order to list books in.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Where the page starts: the previous page's `X-Next-Cursor`. Needs `sort` and `dir`,
set as they were for that page.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to include, such as `m4b,mp3`. Older clients send this;
newer ones put a `format` clause in `filter`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Filter clauses as a percent-encoded JSON array, such as
`[{"field":"format","mode":"include","values":["epub"]}]`. A clause matches a book
when any of its values does, and a book must match every clause. Up to 16 clauses
of up to 64 values each.

parameters.name: exclude_formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to leave out, such as `cbz`: the formats the user hides
from their library view.

parameters.name: stack_series
parameters.description:
Fold each series of two or more books into one row and list the series in `stacks`.
`X-Total-Count` still counts books. Applies to a paged request only.

parameters.name: omit_description
parameters.description: Leave each book's description out, for a lighter page. Applies to a paged request only.

200.description: A page of books, or the whole library.

X-Hidden-Count.description: How many books `exclude_formats` left out. Sent on the first page only.

X-Next-Cursor.description: The `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page, and when the request wasn't paged.

X-Total-Cap.description: The cap, sent when it cut an unpaged response short.

400.description: A `cursor` came without `sort` and `dir`, or a `cursor` or `filter` is malformed.

get.description: One book's full record.

The book's table of contents, with the spine index that
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters/{spine_index}/text` reads each chapter by. A PDF has one
spine entry per page. A book with no EPUB or PDF, such as a comic or an audiobook,
answers `has_text: false` with no chapters.

The plain text of one spine document: an EPUB chapter, or a PDF page. A long chapter
comes in slices of up to 100,000 characters: while `truncated` is set, ask again with
`offset` set to `next_offset`. An `offset` past the end answers an empty slice. A book
with no EPUB or PDF answers `has_text: false`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Where the slice starts, in characters from the start of the chapter. Defaults to 0.
Pass the previous slice's `next_offset` to continue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
The most characters to return, from 1 to 100,000. Defaults to 100,000, and a larger
value is lowered to it.

parameters.name: stop_at_progress
parameters.description:
Cut the text off at your own furthest reading position in this book, so you are never
handed text you haven't reached yet.

200.description: A slice of the chapter's text.

404.description: No book has that uuid, or `spine_index` is past the book's last spine document.

post.description:
Replaces the book's cover with the image in the form's `cover` part. The book's other
metadata edits stay. Answers with the book as it now reads. Needs the edit permission.

cover.description: The image, under 10 MB, with an `image/*` content type. SVG is refused.

200.description: The book with its new cover.

400.description: The form has no `cover` part, the part's content type isn't an image or is SVG, or the image is over 10 MB.

403.description: Your account lacks the edit permission.

415.description: The `cover` bytes aren't in an image format the server recognizes.

delete.description:
Removes a cover you set, so the book shows the cover from its file again. The book's
other metadata edits stay. Answers with the book as it now reads. Needs the edit
permission.

200.description: The book with its scanned cover.

403.description: Your account lacks the edit permission.

post.summary: Set a book's cover from a URL
post.description:
Fetches the image at `url` and makes it the book's cover. For a Google Books cover, the
server stores the full-size image instead of the thumbnail when it can. The book's other
metadata edits stay. Answers with the book as it now reads. Needs the edit permission.

200.description: The book with its new cover.

400.description: `url` is empty, over 2,048 bytes or not `https`, its host resolves to a private address, or it doesn't answer with an image of up to 10 MB.

403.description: Your account lacks the edit permission.

415.description: The URL answered with bytes that aren't an image.

502.description: The server couldn't reach the URL's host.

get.description:
The book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB, as an attachment. `file_id` picks one of
its EPUB or PDF files instead. An EPUB carries your metadata and cover edits. A comic's
archive comes from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/file`. Answers `Range` requests, so an
interrupted download can resume. Needs the download permission.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description:
One of the book's EPUB or PDF files, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`. Leave it
out for the file the route picks by default.

206.description: The byte range asked for in `Range`.

304.description: The file is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

403.description: Your account lacks the download permission.

404.description: No book has that uuid, the book has no EPUB or PDF, `file_id` isn't one of its EPUB or PDF files, or the file is missing from disk.

416.description: The `Range` lies outside the file. `Content-Range` gives its length.

get.description:
The book's EPUB, else its CBZ archive for a comic, else its PDF, served inline for
reading or for taking the book offline. `file_id` picks one of its EPUB or PDF files
instead. Answers `Range` requests. Every response, errors included, carries
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. For a copy with your metadata edits baked in, use
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/download`.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description:
One of the book's EPUB or PDF files, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`. Leave it
out for the file the route picks by default.

206.description: The byte range asked for in `Range`.

304.description: The file is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

404.description: No book has that uuid, the book has no EPUB, CBZ or PDF, `file_id` isn't one of its EPUB or PDF files, or the file is missing from disk.

416.description: The `Range` lies outside the file. `Content-Range` gives its length.

get.description:
Every image in the book's EPUB, such as maps and illustrations, with the spine documents
that show each one.

422.description: The book has no EPUB.

get.summary: Download one of a book's images
get.description:
The image's original file from the book's EPUB, as an attachment. `href` is the image's
path from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images`. Needs the download permission.

parameters.name: href
parameters.description: The image's path inside the EPUB, as `href` in `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images`.

304.description: The image is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

400.description: `href` isn't an image in the book's EPUB.

403.description: Your account lacks the download permission.

422.description: The book has no EPUB.

get.summary: Get a signed link to an image
get.description:
A path that fetches one image's original file without a session for 15 minutes, for
handing to something that can't send your token. It opens that one image and nothing
else. `href` isn't checked against the book's images until the link is used. Needs the
download permission.

parameters.name: href
parameters.description: The image's path inside the EPUB, as `href` in `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images`.

403.description: Your account lacks the download permission.

get.summary: Open an image through a signed link
get.description:
The image a link from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images/link` points at, as an attachment.
The link's signature is its only credential: no session is needed or read. Use the
link's path as it is.

parameters.name: href
parameters.description: The image's path inside the EPUB.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: When the link stops working, in Unix seconds.

304.description: The image is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`, or the date in `If-Modified-Since`.

400.description: `href` isn't an image in the book's EPUB.

401.description: The link has expired, or its signature doesn't match.

422.description: The book has no EPUB.

get.summary: Download a book as a KEPUB
get.description:
The book's EPUB converted to Kobo's KEPUB format, as an attachment named
`{uuid}.kepub.epub`, for copying onto a Kobo over USB. The first request converts the
book, which can take up to 25 seconds. When the conversion fails or runs longer, you get
the plain EPUB, named `{uuid}.epub`, instead. Either file carries your metadata and cover
edits. Needs the download permission.

200.description: The KEPUB, or the plain EPUB.

403.description: Your account lacks the download permission.

404.description: No book has that uuid, or the book has no EPUB or its EPUB is missing from disk.

post.description:
Saves the fields you send over the book's scanned metadata. Fields you leave out keep any
earlier edit, and a list field, such as `creators`, replaces the whole list. Answers with
the book as it now reads. Needs the edit permission.

400.description: A field is too long or malformed. The body says which.

403.description: Your account lacks the edit permission.

delete.description:
Removes every edit to the book, its cover included, so it reads as scanned. Answers with
the book as it now reads. Needs the edit permission.

403.description: Your account lacks the edit permission.

get.description:
One page image from the book's CBZ archive, so you never download or unzip the whole
archive. Pages are numbered from 0 in the archive's natural sort order, the order the
book's `page_count` counts.

304.description: The page is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No book has that uuid, the book has no CBZ, or it has no page with that number.

get.description:
Books that Hardcover's curated lists pair with this one, for a "readers also enjoyed"
strip. `status` is `not_configured` when the server has no Hardcover key, `pending`
while the server fetches them in the background (ask again shortly), or `ready` with
the items, which may be empty. Results are kept for 30 days, then refreshed.

200.description: The suggestions, or why there are none yet.

post.description:
Asks one provider for a summary of the book and returns its text, or `null` when that
provider has none (try the next source from `GET /api/summary/sources`). An unknown
uuid also answers `null`. Nothing is saved. A provider that can't be reached is a 500.
Needs the edit permission.

Rebuilds the index book search reads from the library's current records, and answers
when it is done. Use it when search results don't match the library. Needs an admin
account.

get.description:
Every genre assigned to a book, with the number of books carrying it, most-used
first. Stops at the 500 most-used genres.

get.summary: Get the Google Books key's status
get.description:
Whether a Google Books API key is set, where it comes from, and a masked preview. The
key itself is never returned. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Saves the server-wide Google Books API key, or clears it when `key` is `null`, absent
or blank. With a key, ISBN lookups ask Google Books first; without one, Open Library.
Clearing the saved key falls back to the server's `GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY` environment
variable, when that is set. Needs an admin account.

422.description: The key is longer than 512 bytes.

get.description:
Whether a Hardcover API key is set, where it comes from, and a masked preview. The key
itself is never returned. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Saves the server-wide Hardcover API token, or clears it when `key` is `null`, absent or
blank. The key turns on book suggestions, makes Hardcover the first source for
summaries, and adds it as the last source for ISBN lookups. Clearing the saved key
falls back to the server's `HARDCOVER_API_KEY` environment variable, when that is set.
Needs an admin account.

422.description: The key is longer than 2048 bytes.

post.description:
Highlights a passage of a book. Mint a `client_id` on the device and the create is safe
to repeat: sending the same `client_id` again returns the highlight the first create
made, unchanged.

400.description: `book_uuid` or `epub_cfi_range` is blank, a field is too long, `client_id` is blank, or `client_created_at` is negative.

get.summary: List your highlights in a book
get.description:
Each highlight comes placed in the book: its spine index, chapter title and how far
through the book it sits. Returns up to 1,000, and an empty list for a uuid no book has.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description:
`position` (the default) lists them in reading order through the book, with any the
server can't place last. `chronological` (or `created`) lists them oldest first. Any
other value means `position`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The highlight's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

404.description: You have no highlight with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The highlight's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

404.description: You have no highlight with that id.

patch.description: Replaces the note. A null or absent `note` removes it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The highlight's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

400.description: The note is over 4,096 characters.

404.description: You have no highlight with that id.

post.description:
Writes a markdown entry about a book. A published entry, the default, is visible to
every user under your name; a `draft` only to you. Mint a `client_id` on the device and
the create is safe to repeat: sending the same `client_id` again returns the entry the
first create made, unchanged.

200.description: The entry, with its markdown rendered to HTML.

400.description: `book_uuid` or `body_md` is blank, `body_md` is over 65,536 bytes, `progress` is over 100, `client_id` is blank or too long, or `client_created_at` is negative.

get.description:
Every user's published entries for the book, plus your own drafts, newest first. Returns
up to 1,000, and an empty list for a uuid no book has.

post.description:
Stores an image to embed in a journal entry and returns its URL. Put the URL in the
entry's markdown as `![caption](url)`.

schema.description: The multipart form `POST /api/journals/images` takes: one part, named `image`.

image.description:
The image: JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP, up to 10 MiB. The part's own `Content-Type` must
be an `image/*` type other than SVG.

400.description: The form has no `image` part, or the part's `Content-Type` isn't an image type, is SVG, or the image is over 10 MiB.

415.description: The bytes aren't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image.

get.description:
An image uploaded for a journal entry, by the name at the end of its URL. A name never
points at different bytes, so the response may be cached for a year.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The last segment of the URL the upload returned: a uuid and an extension.

post.description:
Renders markdown to HTML exactly as a saved entry's `body_html` is rendered, so a
composer can show a preview. The request body is the markdown as a JSON string, and the
response the sanitized HTML as a JSON string.

requestBody.description: The markdown, as a JSON string.

200.description: The rendered HTML, as a JSON string.

400.description: The markdown is over 65,536 bytes.

delete.description:
Deletes one of your entries, and any uploaded image it showed that no other entry
shows.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The entry's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

404.description: You have no entry with that id. Another user's entry answers the same.

patch.description:
Replaces the body and progress of one of your entries. Send `status` to publish a draft
or turn an entry back into one; leave it out to keep the status. An uploaded image the
old body showed and no entry shows any more is deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The entry's id, or the `client_id` it was created with.

400.description: `body_md` is blank or over 65,536 bytes, or `progress` is over 100.

404.description: You have no entry with that id. Another user's entry answers the same.

post.summary: Send a book to your Kindle
post.description:
Queues an email of the book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB, to your Kindle
address, and answers before it goes out. Poll `GET /api/kindle/send/status` with the
`task_id` to learn whether it was sent. A file over 50 MB fails there, not here.

409.description: The server has no email delivery set up.

422.description: `book_uuid` is longer than 64 bytes, or you have no Kindle address set.

get.description:
Whether a send from `POST /api/kindle/send` is still going, went out, or failed. Poll
about once a second: a finished send is forgotten 10 seconds after it ends.

404.description: No send of yours has that `task_id`, or it ended more than 10 seconds ago.

get.summary: Count the files in the library folders
get.description:
How many ebook and audiobook files the configured library folders hold, by extension.
It walks the folders on disk, so it counts files a scan hasn't indexed yet. A folder that
is missing or unreadable reports `error` in its section instead of failing the request.

What the whole library is made of: its mix of formats, languages, publishers,
publication decades and genres. The same for every user.

How big the whole library is in words, pages and seconds of audio, with how many books
each figure could measure. The same for every user.

post.description:
Fetches one search candidate again from the provider that offered it, which returns
more than the search did. Answers `null` when the provider no longer knows the
candidate. Send the candidate's `isbn13` when it has one: it names the exact printing.
Needs the edit permission.

400.description: `provider_ref` is blank or longer than 256 bytes, or `isbn13` is longer than 32 characters.

502.description: The provider couldn't be reached, or it rate-limited the server recently and is still cooling down.

post.description:
Asks the metadata providers, all of them or those in `providers`, for editions that
match, and returns every candidate labelled with the provider it came from. Each
provider also gets a row in `sources`: a provider that fails or is skipped says so
there, and the search still succeeds. Send `title`, `author` and `isbn` when you have
them; `query` alone is searched as a title. Needs the edit permission.

200.description: The candidates and each provider's status.

400.description: Every field is blank, a field is too long, or `providers` is an empty list; the body says which.

get.description:
Every external metadata provider the server knows: its name, whether it needs an API
key, whether it can be asked right now, and what it can answer. No key material is
returned.

delete.description:
Deletes one physical copy, say after you sold it. The book stays, even when this was
its last copy: `DELETE /api/physical/{uuid}` removes a book with no files. Only the
reader who checked the copy in, or an admin, can remove it.

403.description: Someone else checked the copy in.

patch.description:
Replaces the copy's free-text note. A `null` or blank note clears it. Only the reader
who checked the copy in, or an admin, can change it.

400.description: The note is longer than 4096 characters.

403.description: Someone else checked the copy in.

delete.summary: Delete a book with no files
delete.description:
Deletes a book that has no digital files, with everything tied to it, such as its
physical copies, wishlist entries and ratings, for every reader. Clients offer it when
the last physical copy goes. Needs the edit permission.

409.description: The book still has digital files.

get.description:
Every physical copy of the book, whoever checked it in, oldest check-in first. An
unknown uuid has no copies, so the list is empty.

get.summary: Get your wishlist entry for a book
get.description: Your physical wishlist entry for the book, or `null` when it isn't on your wishlist.

post.summary: Add a book to your wishlist
post.description:
Adds a book the library already has to your physical wishlist. Adding it again returns
the existing entry. To wishlist a book the library doesn't have, use
`POST /api/scan/wishlist`.

delete.summary: Remove a book from your wishlist
delete.description:
Removing a book that isn't on your wishlist still succeeds. A book that exists only
because someone wanted it (no file, no physical copy, no other reader's entry) is
deleted with its last entry, and `book_deleted` tells you so.

200.description: The entry is gone; whether the book went with it.

post.description:
Records where you are in a book in one format: `epub` with an `epub_cfi`, a
`progress_percent` or both, or `audio` with `audio_position_seconds`. The latest
position wins, judged by `client_updated_at` (the server's clock when absent), so a
write older than the stored position changes nothing. An `audio` position without
`book_file_id` also loses to a stored one that names a file of a multi-file audiobook.
The response is the position the server kept, yours or the stored one.

400.description: The position doesn't fit its format: it is missing or blank, sets a field of the other format, has `progress_percent` outside 0 to 100, a `book_file_id` below 1 or a negative `client_updated_at`, or `book_uuid` is blank.

get.summary: List the books you were last in
get.description:
Your most recent positions, newest first, each with its book: a "pick up where you left
off" list. Send `user_id` for another reader's list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many books to return, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 1; a value outside the range is
moved to the nearest end.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Read another reader's books instead of your own. They must share their stats.

200.description: The most recent positions, newest first.

400.description: `limit` or `user_id` isn't a whole number.

404.description: `user_id` names no reader, or one who doesn't share their stats.

post.description:
Stores a batch of up to 500 reading or listening sessions, each a stretch of time spent
in one book. Sessions for a book the server doesn't know are dropped. Give each session a
`client_id` and a batch is safe to send again: a repeated `client_id` isn't stored twice.
The batch is stored whole or not at all.

400.description: A session is invalid: `book_uuid` is blank, a time is negative, `ended_at` is before `started_at`, `progress_units` is negative, `client_id` or `time_zone` is blank or too long, or `utc_offset_minutes` is outside -720 to 840.

422.description: The batch holds more than 500 sessions.

get.summary: Get your positions in a book
get.description:
Every position you hold in the book, one per format, with which one is furthest and the
cross-format link state. The body is `null` when no book has the uuid, and has empty
`records` when you have never opened the book.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Return only the position in this format. Absent, every format you have a position
in comes back.

200.description: Your positions, or `null` when no book has that uuid.

400.description: `format` is not `epub` or `audio`.

post.description:
Sets your star rating for a book, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps, replacing any rating
you gave it before.

400.description: `book_uuid` is blank, or `stars` is outside 0.5 to 5 or not a whole number of half stars.

get.summary: List other users' ratings of a book
get.description:
Every other user's rating of the book, with their name, newest first. Returns up to
1,000, and an empty list for a uuid no book has.

get.summary: Get your rating for a book
get.description: The body is `null` when you haven't rated the book, or no book has the uuid.

delete.summary: Remove your rating of a book
delete.description: Succeeds whether or not you had rated the book.

204.description: You have no rating for the book.

put.description: Marks a book as unread, reading or finished for you, replacing its previous status.

400.description: `book_uuid` is blank or over 64 bytes.

get.description:
Your read status for the book. The body is `null` when you have never set one, or no
book has the uuid; treat that as `unread`.

post.description:
Scans the ebook library folder for added, changed and removed books, and answers when
the scan is done. Audiobooks aren't scanned; `POST /api/scan-library` covers both
libraries without waiting. Needs an admin account.

409.description: No ebook library path is set.

post.description:
Queues a scan of the ebook and audiobook library folders, whichever are set, and answers
without waiting for them. Needs an admin account.

Records a physical copy of a book the library already has, filed under you, and takes
the book off every reader's wishlist. `isbn` is stored as an ISBN-13, or dropped when
it isn't a valid ISBN. The answer carries the book's current uuid, which differs from
`book_uuid` when that book has been merged into another.

400.description: `book_uuid` is empty or longer than 64 bytes, `isbn` is longer than 32 characters, or `note` is longer than 4096 characters.

get.summary: Check whether a Google Books key is set
get.description:
`true` when the server has a Google Books API key, saved in settings or set in its
environment. Without one, Google Books lookups share an anonymous quota that runs out
quickly, so a client can warn that ISBN lookups may fail.

post.summary: Add a book you have only on paper
post.description:
Creates a book with no files from provider metadata, such as the `online` of a
`not_in_library` outcome, and checks in its first copy under you. The cover at
`cover_url` is downloaded now, from the known provider hosts only; when that fails,
the book has no cover.

400.description: A field of `meta` is too long, or `note` is longer than 4096 characters; the body says which.

post.description:
Looks a scanned or typed ISBN up in the library, then at the metadata providers, and
says what to offer next: `already_owned`, `on_wishlist` (yours), `in_library_unowned`,
`close_match` (a library book with the same title and author, to confirm before
writing anything), `not_in_library` or `unresolved`. Takes an ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, with
or without hyphens.

400.description: The ISBN is empty, longer than 32 characters, or not a valid ISBN.

503.description: No metadata provider could be reached.

post.description:
Matches a result from `POST /api/scan/search` against the library, as
`POST /api/scan/resolve` does for an ISBN, without asking the providers again. The
outcome is never `unresolved`.

400.description: A field of `meta` is too long; the body says which.

post.description:
Searches the metadata providers by free text, for when an ISBN resolves to
`unresolved`. Pass the result the reader picks to `POST /api/scan/resolve-meta`. An
empty list means the providers answered and none matched.

400.description: The query is blank or longer than 200 characters.

503.description: No metadata provider could be reached.

post.summary: Add a scanned book to your wishlist
post.description:
Adds a book to your physical wishlist: a library book by `book_uuid`, or one the
library doesn't have from `meta`, which creates a book with no files to hold the
entry. When both are sent, `book_uuid` wins. A book already on your wishlist stays as
it was.

200.description: The book is on your wishlist.

400.description: Neither `book_uuid` nor `meta` was sent, `book_uuid` is blank or longer than 64 bytes, or a field of `meta` is too long.

get.description:
Books whose title, author or series matches `q`, best match first, up to 50,000.
`X-Total-Count` holds how many books match. With no library folder configured, the
answer is an empty list.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Words to match against titles, authors and series, up to 1,024 bytes. Prefix a word
with `author:` or `series:` to match only that field, or with `tag:` or `genre:` to
keep only books with that tag or genre, such as `author:herbert dune`.

X-Total-Cap.description: The cap, sent when it cut the list short.

400.description: `q` is longer than 1,024 bytes.

get.description:
Chapters whose text holds every word of `q`, best match first, up to 50. Each hit names
the book, the chapter's spine index and title, and quotes an excerpt with the matches in
`[` and `]`. By default a hit past your own reading position is marked as ahead of you;
`spoiler_filter=exclude` leaves it out and counts it in `withheld_ahead`. An empty answer
can carry a `hint` saying why. With no library folder configured, or an empty `q`, the
answer has no hits.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Words to find in the text, up to 1,024 bytes. A chapter matches when it holds every
word.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: Search only this book, by uuid.

parameters.name: book_uuids
parameters.description:
Search only these books: comma-separated uuids, up to 50, such as the books of a
series. Combines with `book_uuid`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most hits to return, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: spoiler_filter
parameters.description: What to do with hits past your own reading position. Defaults to `annotate`.

400.description: `q` is longer than 1,024 bytes.

get.description:
Books, authors, series, tags and genres matching `q`, grouped by kind, up to 5 of each
unless `limit` says otherwise. Each kind's `_total` field counts all its matches. Books
match on title, author and series; the rest on any part of the name.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to search for, up to 1,024 bytes.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most hits per category, from 1 to 500. Defaults to 5.

400.description: `q` is longer than 1,024 bytes.

get.description:
Every series with a book in the library, by name, each with a book count, the first
book's first author and an accent color. Stops at 10,000 series.
One series and its books, in series order.

Where the ebook and audiobook libraries live, and how often the server rescans them.
Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Replaces the library settings and, when an ebook library is set, starts a rescan of it
in the background. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The settings are saved; the body is what is now set.

422.description: A library path is over 4096 bytes, or `scan_interval_hours` is below 1.

get.summary: Check whether the MCP endpoint is on
get.description: Whether the server answers MCP clients at `/mcp`. Needs an admin account.

post.summary: Turn the MCP endpoint on or off
post.description:
Chooses whether the server answers MCP clients at `/mcp`. The change applies to the
next `/mcp` request, with no restart. Needs an admin account.

Chooses whether `POST /api/auth/register` accepts new accounts. Anyone can read the
setting, signed in or not, with `GET /api/auth/registration`. Needs an admin account.

get.description:
Every shelf you can see: your own, every public shelf, and every shelf at all when you
are an admin. Each comes with its book count and up to four member uuids for a cover
mosaic.

post.description:
Creates a shelf you own. A smart shelf needs `match_mode` and at least one rule, and
takes no `book_uuids`. A hand-picked shelf takes no rules, and can start with
`book_uuids`. A `wishlist` shelf can't be created: every reader has one already.

404.description: A uuid in `book_uuids` matches no book.

409.description: You already have a shelf with that name.

422.description: The name, description, rules or `book_uuids` are invalid; the body says which.

get.summary: List the hand-picked shelves holding a book
get.description:
The ids of the hand-picked shelves you can see that hold the book, for a "which shelves
is this on" checklist. An unknown uuid is on no shelf, so the list is empty.

200.description: Ids of the shelves holding the book.

get.summary: List the smart shelves matching a book
get.description:
The ids of the smart shelves you can see whose rules match the book right now. Kept
apart from `GET /api/shelves/containing/{uuid}` because a smart shelf's membership
can't be toggled. An unknown uuid matches nothing, so the list is empty.

200.description: Ids of the smart shelves matching the book.

post.description:
Counts how many books a set of rules would match, out of how many in the library, with
a sample of up to 12 of them. Nothing is saved. Rules on your own data, such as rating
and read status, are matched against yours.

200.description: The match count, the library total and a sample.

422.description: More than 50 rules, an operator the field doesn't take, an empty value, or a value that can't be evaluated; the body says which.

get.description: One shelf's details, with its rules when it is a smart shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

delete.description:
Deletes the shelf, its rules and its list of books; the books stay in the library.
Only the shelf's owner or an admin can delete it, and the Wishlist shelf can't be
deleted.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

patch.description:
Changes the fields you send and leaves the rest. `rules` replaces the whole rule set.
Only the shelf's owner or an admin can change it, and the Wishlist shelf can't be
changed at all.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

409.description: You already have a shelf with that name.

422.description: A field is invalid, or the change would give a hand-picked shelf rules or leave a smart shelf with none; the body says which.

post.description:
Appends books to a hand-picked shelf. A book already on it stays where it is. Every
uuid must match a book, or nothing is added. Only the shelf's owner or an admin can
add books, and the Wishlist shelf can't be edited this way.

204.description: The books are on the shelf.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, it is another reader's private shelf, or a uuid matches no book.

422.description: More than 2000 uuids, or a uuid longer than 64 bytes.

delete.summary: Remove a book from a shelf
delete.description:
Takes the book off a hand-picked shelf. Removing a book that isn't on the shelf, or an
unknown uuid, still succeeds. Only the shelf's owner or an admin can remove books, and
the Wishlist shelf can't be edited this way.

204.description: The book is off the shelf.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

get.description:
The books on a shelf, narrowed by `filter`. A smart shelf lists them in the order
`sort` and `dir` ask for; a hand-picked shelf lists them in the order they were added.
There is no paging: the list stops at 50,000 books.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The order to list a smart shelf's books in. Defaults to `recently_interacted`, as
does a value the server doesn't know. A hand-picked shelf keeps its own order.

parameters.name: dir

Your reading over one period: totals, the daily heatmap, your streak, top authors and

get.description:

creates a fileless book plus its first physical copy.

AdminHealthReport.description:
Full report backing `/admin/health`'s five sections, returned in one
request by `GET /api/admin/health` (REST) / `rpc_get_admin_health`
(web). The web page re-fetches this on a 5-second live-update poll
in addition to its initial page-load fetch.

AdminUserRow.description:
Admin Users-table projection of a `users` row. Extends
[`UserSummary`] with the created timestamp and locked state the admin
table renders, without bloating the login-path summary. No password
fields ever cross the wire.

display_name.description: Presentation name, or `None` when the user hasn't set one.

locked.description:
`true` when the account is currently locked out by repeated failed
logins (`locked_until` is in the future).

AlignmentAudioFile.description: One audio file segment for the lane, in current ordinal order.

chapter_starts.description: Chapter start offsets within this file, seconds from its start.

AlignmentEbook.description:
Text-side lane: total visible chars plus chapter tick positions.
Absent when the structure backfill hasn't reached the book — the
modal then shows the honest low-confidence (linear estimate) notice.

anchor_path.description:
In-document CFI step path (`/4/2/6`) of the chapter's anchor when it
shares its spine item with another chapter, placing a position
between them. `None` for a chapter with its spine item to itself.

percent.description: Whole-book percent where the chapter starts, 0..=100.

spine_index.description:
0-based spine item the chapter starts in. Lets a reading position's CFI
spine step resolve to the same chapter the reader opens, instead of the
rounded whole-book percent that lands one chapter ahead when a boundary
falls inside the rounding window. `#[serde(default)]` so a
payload from a server predating the field still decodes.

AlignmentLink.description:
The stored link as the modal needs it, plus whether the audio set has
drifted since confirmation (mapping paused until re-confirmed).

follow.description:
Follow mode: surfaces resolve the freshest position across both
formats instead of offering prompts.

user_anchors.description: How many "synced here" declarations back the mapping.

AlignmentMatch.description:
How well the two chapter structures matched, for the modal's readout
("12 of 14 chapter names matched").

AlignmentPosition.description:
Current reading position (percent may be absent for a fresh CFI whose
derivation hasn't landed).

AlignmentView.description:
Everything the alignment modal renders for one book, in one read:
the stored link (if any) with its staleness, both timelines' raw
material, and both current positions. The client does the linear
preview arithmetic — it must re-run live as the user changes the
declaration, so shipping raw data beats shipping one precomputed map.

oneOf.description:
Chapter-anchor match statistics for a linked, non-stale book —
`None` when no trustworthy anchoring exists (the linear notice).

anchor_pairs.description:
Matched anchor pairs `(text_frac, audio_frac)` in `0.0..=1.0`, in text order:
the connector threads and anchored preview interpolation the modal draws.

requires the key.

audio_chapter_marks.description:
Usable (titled, non-synthetic) audio chapter marks on the preview timeline.
With `anchor_match` absent on a non-stale view, zero means "no marks in the
audio" and nonzero means "marks exist but couldn't be aligned". On a stale
link the whole preview (this count included) is suppressed at 0; check
`link.stale` before interpreting it.

ApiTokenView.description:
One live API token in the management listing (`GET /api/auth/api-tokens`).
Never carries the secret — that appears exactly once, in
[`CreateApiTokenResponse::secret`].

last_used_at.description: `None` until the token first authenticates a request.

suffix.description:
Last 4 characters of the raw token, for the `omni_…xxxx` display
identifier. `None` on tokens minted before the suffix was recorded.

AttributedRating.description: A rating with the user identity needed for an attributed book-detail row.

has_avatar.description: Whether the rater has an avatar to render in place of their monogram.

stars.description: Star rating in `0.5..=5.0`, in half-star steps.

username.description: The rater's display name, falling back to their username.

AudiobookInspection.description: Tag-derived metadata returned by the audiobook inspect step — the audiobook sibling of [`UploadInspection`].

cover_preview.description:
A small `data:` URL of the first part's embedded art — see
[`UploadInspection::cover_preview`].

creators.description:
Every creator the indexer would record from the tags, `author` first —
the sibling of [`UploadInspection::creators`]. Audio containers carry
one artist tag, so this holds at most that one name today; it is a
list so the form reads both inspections the same way.

duration_seconds.description: Combined runtime across every part, when tags supplied durations.

format.description: Lowercased format the server settled on (`"m4b"`, `"m4a"`, `"mp3"`).

has_cover.description: Whether any uploaded part carried embedded cover art.

part_count.description:
Number of files in the upload (1 for a single `.m4b`/`.m4a`; N for a
multi-part `.mp3` audiobook filed into one folder).

next_file_id.description:
The next `book_files` row in ordinal order, absent on the last
file (and for narrations-linked books, where each file is the
whole book): the player advances here when this file ends
instead of marking the book finished.

per-part URLs for HTTP Range streaming, `hls` is the transcode fallback for
codecs that need conversion. Both carry `book_file_id` (what a progress write
must name) and `audio_file_count` (`> 1`: a position is only meaningful with
its file id); both default to 0, meaning "identity unknown".

AudiobookPlaybackRateRecord.description: Server-authoritative playback-rate preference for one audiobook.

progress.description: How far the transcode has got, from 0.0 to 1.0.

ready.description: Whether the transcode has finished. Older field: read `state` instead.

Where an audiobook's HLS transcode stands: `preparing` while it is queued or running,
`ready` once every segment is made, and `failed` when it failed, which isn't retried on
its own.

AuthorDetail.description:
Author detail payload for `GET /api/authors/:id` and `rpc_get_author`.
Contains the author row plus every book by that author.

has_photo.description: `true` when a usable profile photo is cached for this author (a `manual` or `openlibrary` row in `author_photos`). The frontend hero swaps the letter avatar for `` when set. `'letter'` negative-cache rows do not set this flag.

reading.description:
The caller's state on each of `books` they have opened or marked;
a book absent here is unread with no position.

AuthorPhotoScanResult.description:
Result of an admin-triggered "Scan for picture" run. The endpoint
clears any cached row and runs the Open Library cascade inline; a
`false` here means Open Library had nothing to offer for this author
and a sticky `letter` marker has been written to skip future
autoresolution.

url.description: An `http` or `https` URL of a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image, up to 2048 bytes.

AuthorReading.description:
One reader's progress through one author's books, for the `/authors`
list. Per-reader, so it rides its own request beside [`AuthorSummary`],
which every reader shares. An author the reader never opened is absent.

last_read_at.description: The newest [`BookReading::last_read_at`] across the author's books.

AuthorSummary.description:
Lightweight author row for the `/authors` index. Carries only what the
card needs — no joined book list. The detail page (`AuthorDetail`) is
fetched on click.

accent.description:
Cover-derived accent color borrowed from the author's first book
with a non-null `accent_color`. `None` when no owned book has one
— the UI falls back to the theme accent.

has_photo.description: `true` when a usable profile photo is cached for this author (a `manual` or `openlibrary` row in `author_photos`). BookFileInfo.description:

frontend so the format switcher can offer a file picker when N > 1.

a catalog row is read for "how long is it", not for position arithmetic.

etag.description:
Content validator for this file (see [`crate::file_etag`]). An offline client

learn its copy is stale. `None` for rows the scanner has not stat'd yet, so the

path.description:
Library-relative path (`book_files.scan_key`, e.g.
`clarke/piranesi.epub`) — what the delete dialog shows so an admin can
see exactly which file on disk a row stands for. `None` for rows
predating the `scan_key` backfill.

size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of this file. Lets the per-file Send-to-Kindle rows gate
oversized EPUBs the same way the hero export menu does.

BookImage.description: One image in an EPUB's manifest.

byte_size.description: Uncompressed size in bytes, from the archive's directory.

book's EPUB.

BookImageReference.description: One spine document that shows an image.

alt.description: The `` text at the document's first use; `None` when absent or blank, and always for an SVG ``.

spine_index.description: Index into the spine, as in the chapter listing.

necessarily the one asked for, which may be a merged-away uuid.

reader or player (and file) it was left in. `None` without a position.

percent.description: Whole-book percent of the latest position, floored; `None` without one.

Co-listing count — how many curated Hardcover lists co-shelve this book

One superlative that names a book: which book won, and the figure it won with.

Set when the slice was cut at the reader's own furthest position rather than at
[`CHAPTER_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`] (the `?stop_at_progress=true` contract). `truncated`
stays `false` and `next_offset` is absent: there is no cursor to continue from.

CheckInRequest.description: Check in a physical copy of a book already in the library.

allOf.description: Payload for creating a new bookmark.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at the moment of the gesture, so an
offline client can address this bookmark before the server has assigned
it a numeric id. Creates are idempotent on it.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateBookmark.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

allOf.description: Payload for creating a new highlight.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at the moment of the gesture, so an
offline client can address this highlight before the server has
assigned it a numeric id. Creates are idempotent on it, which also
makes a replayed create safe to retry.

text.description:
The selected prose at creation time. Optional so older clients (and
the mobile REST body) can omit it.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateHighlight.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

allOf.description:
Write payload: create a new journal entry on a book. `status` defaults to
`published` so pre-drafts mobile clients keep their old behaviour.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at composition time, so an offline client
can edit or delete this entry before the server has assigned it an id.
Creates are idempotent on it.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateJournalEntry.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

CompositionDimension.description:
One dimension of the library's composition: its buckets plus the coverage
behind them. `coverage.total` is **bucket placements** (the sum of every
slice's `books`) and `coverage.books` the **distinct live books** the
dimension describes; they differ when a book lands in several buckets.
`coverage.books == 0` means no book carries this dimension: show an empty state.

CompositionSlice.description:
One bucket of a [`LibraryComposition`] dimension: a display label and the
distinct live books behind it.

ConfirmCrossFormatLink.description:
The confirm write: the user's declaration for one book. `audio_order`
(when present) persists a re-ordering of the audio files' ordinals —
library-wide data, so the server gates it on edit permission.

ContentSearchHit.description: One content-search hit: a chapter-level citation plus a match excerpt.

ahead_of_reader.description:
Whether this hit sits past the reader's furthest recorded position in
its book. `None` when the reader has no position there, or when the
book's structure is not extracted enough to place the hit — which is
**not** the same as "safe", and a caller must not render it as such.

chapter_title.description:
TOC title of the chapter the match came from, when the book's
structure has been extracted. Saves every caller repeating the same
spine-index-to-chapter join by hand.

position_delta_percent.description:
How far past (positive) or behind (negative) the reader this hit is,
in whole-book percentage points. `None` on the same terms as
[`Self::ahead_of_reader`].

snippet.description:
FTS5 `snippet()` excerpt: matched terms wrapped in `[`…`]`, elided
context marked with `…`.

spine_index.description: Zero-based spine position of the chapter the match came from.

title.description: The book's display title, for rendering the citation.

ContentSearchResults.description: Response body for `GET /api/search/content`, best-ranked hit first.

hint.description:
Why an empty result set is empty, when the query form is the likely
cause. The index matches all terms, so a natural-language phrase
usually matches nothing while its individual words match plenty —
and without this the caller has no reason to suspect the query
rather than the corpus.

withheld_ahead.description:
How many hits `SpoilerFilter::Exclude` held back. Always present
under that mode (`0` when nothing was withheld) so a caller can say
"there is an answer ahead of you" honestly; absent otherwise.

Contributor.description:
A contributor (or creator) with the optional OPF refinements: the MARC role
code (`aut`, `ill`, `edt`, `bkp`, `trl`, …) and the sort-key name.

`id` is the `authors.id` primary key, set when loaded from a m2m join and
`None` for contributors created by the EPUB parser before indexing.

url.description:
The image to fetch, up to 2,048 bytes long. Only `https` URLs on public addresses
are fetched.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`. `secret` is the raw `omni_…`
token, shown to the client exactly once — the server keeps only its hash,
so it is unrecoverable afterward. Deliberately does not derive `Debug`,
same as `LoginRequest`: a stray `tracing::debug!(?resp)` must not leak a
long-lived credential.

CreateBookmark.description: Payload for creating a new bookmark.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at the moment of the gesture, so an
offline client can address this bookmark before the server has assigned
it a numeric id. Creates are idempotent on it.

CreateHighlight.description: Payload for creating a new highlight.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at the moment of the gesture, so an
offline client can address this highlight before the server has
assigned it a numeric id. Creates are idempotent on it, which also
makes a replayed create safe to retry.

text.description:
The selected prose at creation time. Optional so older clients (and
the mobile REST body) can omit it.

CreateJournalEntry.description:
Write payload: create a new journal entry on a book. `status` defaults to
`published` so pre-drafts mobile clients keep their old behaviour.

client_id.description:
Identity minted on the device at composition time, so an offline client
can edit or delete this entry before the server has assigned it an id.
Creates are idempotent on it.

CreateShelfRequest.description:
Create payload. For smart: `match_mode` + `rules` set, `book_uuids` empty.
For manual: `match_mode`/`rules` empty, `book_uuids` optional.

CreateUserRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/users` (admin create). See
[`LoginRequest`] for why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

CrossFormatCandidate.description:
One mapped resume position. The audio-half fields are set when
`target` is audio; `percent` when the target is the ebook.

epub_cfi.description:
Server-derived point CFI at the mapped fraction, present only when
the caller asked (`?derive=cfi`): the web reader displays it
directly, so the fraction is never reinterpreted on epub.js's
different locations scale. Absent on audio targets and on
derivation failure — `fraction` remains the fallback.

fraction.description:
Full-precision position fraction (`0.0..=1.0`) for epub-target
candidates: the jump destination; `percent` is its floored display
twin. Absent on audio targets, whose seconds already carry
precision.

source_ahead.description:
Whether the mapped source position sits ahead of the target's own
current position — `Some(false)` marks a backward offer (the source
regressed), so prompt copy must not claim "further". `None` when
the target has no comparable position (treat as ahead).

source_client_updated_at.description:
Ordering clock (client event time) of the source row, so clients
can de-duplicate prompts against positions they already know.

source_format.description: The format the position was mapped from.

source_position_seconds.description:
The source listening row's own position as global timeline seconds
— the reader banner's "you listened to ≈ 16h 05m" copy. Epub
targets only.

target.description: The format this candidate resumes (the request's `?target=`).

CrossFormatLinkMode.description:
How a book's multiple audio files relate — declared by the user when
confirming a link, never guessed.

CrossFormatResume.description: Response shape of the cross-format resume read.

follow.description:
Follow mode on the link: a `Candidate` should be applied silently
(resolve-at-read) instead of offered as a prompt.

CrossFormatResumeState.description: Why (or whether) the endpoint has a candidate to offer.

DailyGoal.description:
One reader's standing daily goal for one kind, with today's progress toward
it. Recurring, so there is no `year`: `day` names the day `current` was
measured over. Both kinds measure the same day: today on the reader's
calendar (the client's declared offset, else their latest session's, else
UTC).

current.description:
Progress toward `target` on `day`. May exceed it, for the reason
[`ReadingGoal::current`] may.

day.description:
The day `current` was measured over, `YYYY-MM-DD`. See the type docs
for which calendar that is.

target.description:
The target the reader set. Always `>= 1`; a cleared goal is an absent
[`DailyGoal`], never a zero target.

DailyGoalUpdate.description:
Write payload for `PUT /api/stats/goal/daily`. A separate route and type from
[`ReadingGoalUpdate`], whose `Option<ReadingGoal>` response shipped iOS
builds already decode. `kind` is required, as a reader may be setting either
of two goals. An absent `target` **clears** that kind, like
[`ReadingGoalUpdate::target`].

DailyGoals.description:
A reader's daily goals — at most one per kind, each independent of the
other and of the annual [`ReadingGoal`].

oneOf.description: The minutes goal, `None` when unset.

minutes_today.description:
Minutes read and listened today, whether or not a minutes target is set,
over the same day as [`Self::pages_today`]. Truncating, like the minutes
goal's own `current`: 59 seconds is not yet a minute.

oneOf.description: The pages goal, `None` when unset.

pages_today.description:
Pages covered today, measured whether or not a pages target is set:
the same figure [`DailyGoal::current`] carries, so setting a target
never moves it. `None` only when the server could not measure it,
never as a stand-in for zero.

unzoned_seconds.description:
Always `0`, kept so a client built against the earlier shape still
decodes. The day is placed by the reader's current offset, not each
session's, so every session counts toward [`Self::minutes_today`] and
nothing is left unplaced to disclose.

DayActivity.description:
One heatmap cell: a calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD` on the reader's calendar)
and the total active seconds recorded that day across reading and listening.

DeclareSyncPoint.description:
One "synced here" declaration: the declaring surface names its own
position; the counterpart half of the anchor pair comes from the
