server's stored row for the other format at declaration time.

audio_book_file_id.description: Listening surface: the playing file and seconds within it.

epub_cfi.description:
Reading surface, optional precision upgrade: the reader's current
CFI. When present the server derives the anchor fraction from it on
its own spine-stats ruler, overriding `ebook_fraction` (which the
web reader measures on epub.js's different locations scale).

DeleteBookFilesRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/books/{uuid}/delete-files`: the `book_files`
ids and physical-copy ids to remove. Either list may be empty; both empty
on a book with no items at all deletes the record.

book_deleted.description:
True when the book row itself was removed, so the caller must navigate
away instead of refetching a page that no longer exists.

DeviceView.description:
A registered device row as shown to its owner or an admin. Shared by the
admin `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/devices` listing (self-service devices
are deferred — see `/api/auth/devices` note in the PR body).

DownloadFormat.description:
Which of a book's two downloadable formats a validator query is about.
The wire form is the same token the client's download registry uses.

DownloadValidator.description:
The answer to one query. `etag` is `None` when the book, the format, or
the chosen file is gone, or when the scanner has not stat'd it — all of
which a client reads as "can't tell", never as "unchanged".

DownloadValidatorQuery.description: One "what is this file's validator now?" question.

file_id.description:
The explicitly chosen `book_files` row, when the download was started
against one. `None` means whichever row the server resolves by
default, so a book with two editions is answered about the same file
the download actually came from.

total.description:
Total FTS5 hit count *before* the server-side `MAX_BOOKS_RETURNED` cap,
set by the search paths so the web client can show "N of M results"
even when `books` is truncated. `None` for the full-library
(`/api/ebooks`, `rpc_get_ebooks`) responses, which surface truncation
via the `X-Total-Count` header instead.

EbookMetadata.description:
Parsed metadata for a single ebook file.

`cover_url` is a relative URL to `/api/covers/:id` when the book has a cover;
clients combine it with their configured server base. OPF
`<dc:contributor>` entries are merged into `creators` (creators first).

accent.description:
Cover-derived accent color. Opaque CSS color value extracted
during indexing. `None` means "no cover or extraction failed" —
the frontend falls back to the theme default accent.

added_at.description:
Row insertion timestamp from `books.timestamp` — SQLite
`datetime('now')` format (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, UTC, space separator).
Drives the "Newest Added" sort — distinct from `modified` (DC
last-write).

book_files.description:
Every `book_files` row on this book, one per file on disk, including ordinary
single-file books. Each row carries that file's content validator
(`BookFileInfo::etag`) for offline staleness checks; count rows per format
rather than reading emptiness as a proxy. Empty only on the list projection,
which does not join this table.

description.description:
Sanitized HTML. `None` on browse rows — `LibraryPage.books`, their stack
members, and keyset `/api/ebooks` pages sent `omit_description=true` —
which never carry it: absent there is not empty, so read the book's
detail for it.

epub_size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of the file the hero "Send to Kindle" would deliver (the
lowest-ordinal EPUB, else the PDF). `None` when the book has neither.
Drives the oversized-file gate on the email button — see
`kindle_email_oversize`.

genres.description:
User-assigned genres. Unlike `subjects` (which the EPUB OPF supplies
via `<dc:subject>`), no file format Omnibus reads carries a genre, so
this list is sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — there is no
scanned baseline to revert to and no canonical link table behind it.

has_cover_override.description: True when `cover_url` is a user-uploaded override cover, not the scanned original.

has_override.description:
True when user-supplied metadata overrides are active for this book.
The detail page uses this to show a "has overrides" indicator and
offer a revert action.

has_physical.description: Whether the book has ≥1 physical copy checked in (drives the physical badge).

isbn10.description:
Secondary ISBN-10, sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — no
file format Omnibus reads carries a distinct ISBN-10 alongside its
ISBN-13, so unlike `isbn13` there is no scanned baseline underneath
this one.

isbn13.description:
Primary ISBN-13: derived from whichever `identifiers` entry (in
DB-projection order, not original OPF scan order) has a scheme
mentioning "isbn" and a value that normalizes to 13 ASCII digits, or
a user override from `metadata_overrides` layered on top at read
time. `None` when neither source has one.

last_interacted_at.description:
Most recent moment *anyone* interacted with the book — rated it,
published a journal entry, changed its read status, added it to the
library, edited its metadata or cover, or checked in a physical copy.
Fixed-width ISO, so it sorts lexicographically. Drives the "Recently
Interacted" sort; `None` only for a book carrying no signal at all.

page_count.description:
Page count of the CBZ archive `/api/ebooks/{uuid}/pages/{n}` would
serve, so the comic pager can render a slider and map progress onto
page indices. `None` for an EPUB-only book, a malformed archive, or
a row not yet backfilled since being indexed.

print_pages.description:
User-supplied print edition page count, sourced entirely from
`metadata_overrides`. Distinct from `page_count`, the CBZ archive's *image*
count that drives a comic's page slider: this is bibliographic metadata about
a print edition and can coexist with it.

series_id.description:
Stable `series.id` primary key from the normalized DB. Set when the
book was loaded from a join; `None` for books not in any series.

unique_identifier.description:
OPF unique identifier (`<dc:identifier id="…">`). Used by the
frontend to construct `/books/:uuid` and `/api/covers/:uuid` URLs.

stacks.description:
The series folded into one row each. Absent unless the request set `stack_series`
and the page held a series of two or more books.

EbookPage.description:
One response of `GET /api/ebooks`: a page of books, plus the series it folded into
stacks when the request set `stack_series`.

EditionHydrateRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/metadata/editions/hydrate`, the second call the picker
makes once a candidate is selected, naming one edition rather than a query.

`provider_ref` is echoed back exactly as the search handed it over; Omnibus
never parses it, so it is capped rather than validated for shape.

isbn13.description:
The candidate's ISBN-13, when it has one.

Optional because a candidate may have none; `provider_ref` is the re-fetch
handle. When present it is still preferred, since it names a *printing*
where a bare handle may name a work.

isbn.description:
An ISBN the caller already holds for this book, in any format — it is
normalized (and a bad one discarded) server-side.

The strongest signal there is, and the one the old flat query threw
away even when the edit form had it sitting in a field.

providers.description:
Which providers to ask. Absent means every configured one; this is the
hook a provider-filter UI plugs into without a wire change.

query.description:
The query as free text — what the reader sees in the search box, and
the whole request from a client that sends nothing else.

title.description:
The book's title on its own, when the caller can separate it. Lets each
provider be asked in *its* terms: Open Library searches the author's name
inside the title field if handed one flattened string. Absent means "the
reader typed something specific": treat [`Self::query`] as the title, with
no author.

EditionSearchResponse.description:
Fan-out search results: the candidates every asked provider returned, plus
one status row per provider considered — including the ones that were
skipped or failed, which is why a caller can render "Hardcover: couldn't
reach it" instead of quietly showing a shorter list.

ExternalBookMeta.description:
Normalized book metadata resolved from an external provider. Every field but
`isbn13`, `title`, and `source` is best-effort — providers disagree on which
they carry. `cover_url` is a provider-hosted image the caller fetches only
when a book/wishlist entry is actually created, not at lookup time.

first_publish_year.description:
Year the *work* was first published, across all editions — distinct
from `year`, which is this edition's own date.

isbn13.description: The normalized ISBN-13 that resolved (always 13 digits, no hyphens).

series.description:
Series statement as the provider reports it (free text, e.g.
"The Kingkiller Chronicle (1)"). Best-effort Open Library enrichment.

year.description: Publication year or date as the provider reports it (free text).

FileBytes.description:
A file's raw bytes, such as an image, an EPUB or an audio part. Never JSON: the
operation's content type says what the bytes are.

FinishedBook.description:
A book completed within the window — a 100% journal entry or an explicit
read-status `finished`. `finished_at` is the most recent such moment
(unix secs).

cover_url.description:
`/api/covers/:uuid` when the book has a cover, `None` otherwise — same
shape as `EbookMetadata::cover_url`, so the drill-in's finished-books
list can hand it straight to `CoverTile`.

finished_at_iso.description:
[`Self::finished_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC.

Both forms travel together: the epoch is what clients compare and sort
on, the string is what a reader of the API can act on without doing
calendar arithmetic by hand. Populated by the server's read paths.

rating.description: The user's star rating for this book (0.5..=5.0), `None` if unrated.

FtsHealth.description:
`books_fts` vs `books` row-count parity. A rebuild
(`POST /api/fts/rebuild`) always restores `in_sync`; drift here means a
post-commit FTS update failed silently on some earlier write.

GenreShare.description:
One genre-donut slice: a genre and how many distinct books carrying it had
session activity in the window (share by book count, not seconds).

The server sends every genre, not a top-N, so the donut can size its
"Other" fold over the real tail instead of over a silently truncated one.

GenreWeight.description:
One genre with the number of books carrying it. Structurally a
[`TagWeight`], kept a distinct type so `/api/genres` and `/api/tags`
don't share a wire name for two different vocabularies.

GoogleBooksKeyStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide Google Books key for the Settings UI.
**Never carries the raw key** — only a short masked preview. Mirrors
[`crate::suggestion::HardcoverKeyStatus`].

masked.description: Short masked preview (e.g. `AIza…9f3a`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective key comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

HardcoverKeyStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide Hardcover key for the Settings UI. **Never
carries the raw key** — only a short masked preview.

masked.description: Short masked preview (e.g. `hc_l…3f9a`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective key comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

Health.description: A running server's liveness and build details.

app.description: Always `omnibus`, which tells this server apart from another program on the port.

build_id.description:
When this server process started, in Unix milliseconds. It changes on every restart,
so a new value means a rebuilt server is up.

repo_root.description:
The directory the server runs from. Development tooling uses it to tell the servers of
two checkouts apart.

time.description: The server's clock in Unix seconds, so a client can measure how far its own clock is off.

version.description: The release, such as `v0.9.3`, or `dev` for a local build.

Highlight.description:
A persisted highlight annotation.

`PartialEq` but not `Eq`: `percent_through_book` is a float.

chapter_title.description:
TOC title of the chapter it sits in, when the book's structure has
been extracted.

client_id.description:
The device-minted identity this highlight was created under, when the
creating client supplied one. `None` for rows predating migration 0051
and for clients that don't mint one.

created_at_iso.description:
[`Self::created_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When it was made.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

epub_cfi_range.description:
The range CFI the readers paint. A Kobo-origin annotation gets one
derived server-side from its `KoboSpan` location (at ingest, else at
the boot backfill); `None` only while that mapping fails, and such a
row lists in the UI but cannot be placed or jumped to in the web reader.

percent_through_book.description:
How far through the book it sits, 0..=100. Spine-granular — it
measures to the start of the containing spine document, which is what
the stored structure records.

spine_index.description:
Spine document this anchor sits in, resolved from its CFI. `None`
when no CFI could be derived (an unmapped Kobo-origin anchor) or the
CFI is unparseable.

text.description:
The highlighted prose. `None` for highlights created before the text
column shipped (migration 0030).

HourBucket.description:
One column of the time-of-day strip: an hour of the reader's **local** day
and the active seconds recorded in it, reading and listening together.
`hour` is 0..=23 on the reader's own clock, resolved server-side from the UTC
offset each session carried at capture (`db::stats::patterns`), never the
viewing client's zone. [`StatsSummary::hour_of_day`] carries all 24, zeros included.

HouseholdReader.description: One reader in the household listing (`GET /api/users`).

has_avatar.description: Whether `GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` has an image to serve.

id.description: User id; pass it as `user_id` to the stats reads.

is_you.description: True for the signed-in caller, who is always listed first.

Identifier.description: A typed identifier from the OPF, e.g. `{ scheme: "ISBN", value: "…" }`.

IndexStatus.description: Library index summary: configured library paths and row counts.

JournalEntry.description:
A persisted journal entry as rendered for display. `body_html` is the
server-rendered, sanitized markdown; `body_md` is the raw source (the owner
edits it). `created_at` / `updated_at` are unix seconds.

author_has_avatar.description: Whether the author has an avatar to render in place of their monogram.

author_name.description: The author's display name, falling back to their username.

client_id.description:
The device-minted identity this entry was created under, when the
creating client supplied one. `None` for rows predating migration 0051.

created_at_iso.description:
[`Self::created_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When the entry was written.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

updated_at_iso.description:
[`Self::updated_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When it was last edited.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

JournalImageUpload.description:
Response for a journal image upload: the serving URL to embed in the
entry's markdown (`![caption](url)`).

JournalStatus.description:
Publication state of a journal entry: owner-private `Draft` vs shared-feed
`Published` (the default, so pre-drafts clients/rows keep their behaviour).

KindleSendQueued.description: A Send to Kindle that is queued to go out.

task_id.description: Pass this to `GET /api/kindle/send/status` to follow the send.

KindleSendRequest.description: The book to email to your Kindle address.

book_uuid.description: The book's uuid, at most 64 bytes.

file_id.description:
The `id` of one of the book's `book_files`, for a book with several. Leave it out to
send the book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB.

KindleSendStatus.description:
Terminal-or-pending status of a Send-to-Kindle job, returned by the
`kindle/send/status` poll endpoint keyed on the `task_id` that the enqueue
call handed back. The send runs on the background worker; the client posts
once, then polls this until it flips off `Pending`. `Failed.message` is the
per-case reason surfaced to the button toast.

LengthBucket.description:
One bar of the book-length distribution: a page-range label and how many
books finished in the window fall into it. The server owns the boundaries and
labels (`db::stats::pages`). One bucket is the **unknown** bucket (a book no
rung of the length ladder can measure, e.g. an audiobook); render it, don't
drop it, or the distribution covers fewer books than the window.

LibraryComposition.description:
What the collection is made of: its format mix, language mix, publisher
spread, publication-decade histogram, and genre distribution.

**Library-scoped, not user-scoped**, like [`LibrarySize`]. Every count is
`DISTINCT` over books, never rows: a twelve-part M4B is twelve `book_files` rows.

books.description:
Live books — those with at least one surviving `book_files` row. The
denominator every dimension's coverage is read against, and the same
population [`LibrarySize::books`] counts.

decades.description:
Publication decades, oldest first, and **not folded**: a histogram sorted by
height or truncated is a bar chart of nothing. The year uses the same
extraction as smart-shelf rules, so a decade bar and a `year >= 1990` shelf
never disagree. There is no `Unknown` bucket: a book with an absent or
unparseable `pubdate` is uncovered, reported through the coverage pair.

formats.description:
Format mix by `book_files.format`, most books first. A book held in
two formats is counted **once in each bucket** — it really is both —
so the slices sum to `formats.coverage.total`, which exceeds `books`
by exactly the dual-format overlap.

genres.description:
Genre distribution, tail folded into "Other".

**Read its coverage before its slices.** Genres live only in
`metadata_overrides -> '$.genres'`, so this describes just the books someone
has hand-edited, not "your library's genres".

ghosted_books.description:
Books whose files are gone: a `books` row with no surviving `book_files`.

Reported rather than dropped: they carry no format, so they would vanish from
the format rollup and leave per-format counts failing to reconcile. The
identity surfaces publish is `books + ghosted_books` = every `books` row.

languages.description:
Language mix by `languages.code`, tail folded into "Other". Books with
no language link are uncovered rather than bucketed as unknown — an
absent link means the file never declared one.

publishers.description: Publisher spread by `publishers.name`, tail folded into "Other".

LibrarySection.description:
One half of the library listing (either ebooks or audiobooks).

`counts_by_ext` is an ordered list of `(extension, count)` pairs for the
extensions the caller asked the scanner to track, in the caller's order.

LibrarySize.description:
How big the library is in the units a reader thinks in: words, pages, and
hours of audio. **Library-scoped, not user-scoped**: the same for every
reader, so deliberately not a field on [`StatsSummary`].

books.description:
Live books: those with at least one surviving `book_files` row. The
denominator every coverage figure below is read against.

Ghosted books (a `books` row whose files are gone) are excluded from this
*and* from every numerator, since nothing can measure them.

listening_seconds.description:
Total seconds of audio, summed over the parts of the format the server
would actually serve for each book — every volume of it, not one file.
A book with any unprobed part is unmeasured rather than partly counted.

pages.description:
Total pages, resolved per book through the one length ladder in
`db::stats::pages` — a print-edition count, else a comic's exact
image-page count, else the EPUB word estimate.

words.description: Total words across books with a stored `word_count`.

LoginRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/login`.

Deliberately does not derive `Debug`: the struct holds a plaintext
password, and a stray `tracing::debug!(?req)` would write it to logs.

client_kind.description:
Optional — when present, server issues a bearer session instead of a
cookie session and includes the raw token in the response.

LoginResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/register`.
`token` is populated only for bearer (mobile) sessions; cookie sessions
return the cookie in a `Set-Cookie` header and `token` is `None`.

ManifestPart.description: One part of an audiobook in the direct-play manifest.

MappingConfidence.description:
The tier that produced a mapped position. Linear is the v1 floor;
chapter-anchored lands as a sibling variant.

MatchMode.description: How smart conditions combine: `Any` = OR, `All` = AND.

McpStatus.description:
Whether the hosted `/mcp` endpoint is enabled; the body of
`GET`/`POST /api/settings/mcp` and the matching rpc pair. Mirrors
`RegistrationStatus`'s shape for the other instance-level switch.

MeasuredTotal.description:
A library-scale total and the coverage behind it.

`total` and `books` travel as a pair: a total published without its
denominator reports a partly-backfilled library as a smaller one. `books == 0`
means nothing has been measured, which surfaces render as an empty state.

books.description: Books that contributed to `total`. Always `<= LibrarySize::books`.

MergeBooksRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/books/merge`: merge the source book into the target.

MergeBooksResult.description:
Result of a successful merge: the audit-log id (the undo handle) and
the surviving book's uuid.

MetadataOverrides.description:
User-supplied metadata overrides, JSON-serialized into the
`metadata_overrides.overrides` column. Each field, when `Some`, replaces the
scanned value at read time; M2M fields (`creators`, `subjects`, `genres`)
replace the whole list rather than appending.

creators.description: Replaces the entire creators list when present.

genres.description:
Replaces the entire genres list when present. Unlike every other
field here this is not an *override* of a scanned value — nothing
scans a genre — so this key is the sole storage for a book's genres.

isbn10.description:
ISBN-10 override. Same empty-string-clears convention as `isbn13`; a
non-empty value must be exactly 10 characters — 9 digits plus a
check-digit position that is a digit or `X` — enforced by `validate`.

isbn13.description:
ISBN-13 override. `Some("")` clears any scanned/prior-override value
(mirrors the empty-string-clears convention used by the other scalar
fields); a non-empty value must be exactly 13 ASCII digits, enforced
by `validate`.

print_pages.description:
Print page count override. Like `genres`, nothing Omnibus scans
carries a print page count — `books.page_count` is a different thing
entirely (the CBZ image count, migration `0063`) — so this field is
named `print_pages` rather than `page_count` to keep the two
unambiguous on `EbookMetadata`, where both eventually land.

subjects.description: Replaces the entire subjects (tags) list when present.

MetadataProvider.description: Which external provider a lookup resolved against.

MonthCount.description: One month's finished-book count in the trailing-12-month trend chart.

month.description: Calendar month on the reader's calendar, `YYYY-MM`.

PagesReadDetail.description:
What the Pages tile could and could not measure in the window, and the day
before which it cannot measure anything at all. The headline has three
different empty states: no activity, listening only (audio has no page
analogue, so zero pages is *correct*), and reading in books whose length no
rung of the ladder resolves.

audio_books.description:
Distinct books listened to in the window. Audiobooks contribute no
pages by design; this is what separates "listened, so zero pages" from
"nothing happened".

daily.description:
Pages per day on the reader's calendar within the window, active days
only, ascending — the tile's drill-in trend.

measured_books.description: Distinct books that contributed measured page progress in the window.

since_day.description:
UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` the forward-progress ledger began recording. Reading
before it left no position trail to difference and is unrecoverable, so
a window reaching back past this date is reporting on part of itself —
which the surfaces state outright rather than leaving as an unexplained
discontinuity.

unmeasured_books.description:
Distinct books read in the window whose length no rung of the ladder
resolves — real reading the total cannot include.

window_predates_ledger.description:
Whether this window opens before [`Self::since_day`], so part of it is
unmeasurable no matter what the reader did. Computed server-side against the
window's real start, not inferred from the [`StatsRange`]: only the server
knows where a period starts (a Year window just after the epoch is fully
covered, a Week window right after it is not).

PaletteAuthorHit.description: Author hit for the search palette.

book_count.description: Number of books by this author in the active library.

lead_book_title.description:
Title of this author's first book in the library (by sort order),
used for the "incl. <title>" line on the results page. `None` when
the author has no resolvable book title.

PaletteBookHit.description:
Slim book hit for the search palette. No description, no identifiers,
no subjects — just what the result row needs to render.

author_display.description: Pre-joined author names (e.g. "Grace Hopper, Margaret Hamilton").

has_physical.description:
Whether a physical copy is checked in. `formats` says only whether a
file exists, and a paper-only book has none — the check-in picker
needs both to word its confirm. Defaulted so an older payload decodes.

uuid.description:
Stable UUID — what the frontend should use to construct
`/books/:uuid` and `/api/covers/:uuid` URLs.

year.description: Four-digit year extracted from `pubdate`, if present.

PaletteGenreHit.description:
Genre hit for the search palette. Carries no `id` — unlike a tag, a genre
has no navigable row to link to: migration `0066` gives the vocabulary a
`genres` table but no memberships, so the only thing to do with one is
refine the query to `genre:<name>`.

book_count.description: Number of books carrying this genre in the active library.

name.description:
The canonical spelling `materialize_genre_rows` coined, so a library
holding both "sci-fi" and "Sci-Fi" reports one row (matching
`get_genre_cloud`).

PaletteResults.description:
Search-palette response — grouped results with server-side timing.

Each category is capped at 5 hits server-side. The slim per-hit types
(`PaletteBookHit` etc.) carry only display data — no N+1 joins for
description / identifiers / subjects.

book_total.description: True match counts per category, before the 5-hit display cap.

genres.description:
`#[serde(default)]` for the same reason as the totals below, and one
that bites harder: the native iOS client decodes this payload and
predates the field.

PaletteSeriesHit.description: Series hit for the search palette.

author_display.description: Primary author of the first book in the series, if any.

lead_book_title.description:
Title of the first book in the series (by sort order), used for the
"incl. <title>" line on the results page. `None` when the series has
no resolvable book title.

PaletteTagHit.description: Tag hit for the search palette.

book_count.description: Number of books with this tag in the active library.

PeriodComparison.description:
Scalar aggregates for the **same elapsed slice** of the preceding period —
feeds each metric tile's drill-in delta. The current window is
period-to-date, so this is month-to-date against the same days last month
rather than against the whole of it. `Default` (all zero / `None`) for
[`StatsRange::AllTime`], which has no prior window to compare against.

pages_read.description:
Pages read over the baseline window. Day-grained, unlike its siblings
here — the ledger is resolved to days on the reader's calendar — so the
baseline includes the whole of its boundary day, matching the current
window's own partial today.

PhysicalCopy.description:
A physical copy of a book, seen library-wide (shared by all users like a
digital file) but changed only by the reader who filed it — see
[`Self::can_change`]. A book can have many; each is individually deletable.

added_by_name.description:
That user's display name (username when unset), for "checked in by".
`None` when the account is gone or on a payload a client built itself.

added_by_user_id.description: User who checked the copy in; `None` if that account was later deleted.

checked_in_at_iso.description:
[`Self::checked_in_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When the copy was checked in.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

isbn.description: Scanned ISBN for this copy; `None` for a manual (non-scan) add.

note.description: Free-text edition/publisher note until an edition-metadata provider exists.

PositionConfidence.description:
How far a [`ResolvedPosition`]'s chapter attribution can be trusted.
Reported rather than withheld: a coarse answer a caller knows is coarse
beats an absent block it fills in by guessing.

ProgressFormat.description:
Discriminator for the format-specific payload variant in [`ProgressUpdate`]
/ [`ProgressRecord`] / [`SessionReport`]. Serializes as a plain
lowercase string (`"epub"` / `"audio"`) so the wire shape stays compact.

ProgressRecord.description:
Server-authoritative position returned by `POST /api/progress` and
`GET /api/progress/{uuid}`. The non-discriminated field for the other format
is always `None`. `updated_at` is unix seconds of server receipt;
`client_updated_at` is the event time most-recent-wins resolves on (clamped
to server now for a fast clock; server now when the write carried none).

book_file_id.description:
The `book_files` row the position was taken in; see
[`ProgressUpdate::book_file_id`].

derived_epub_cfi.description:
A point CFI for an epub row that stores a whole-book percent but no CFI (a
Kobo's percent-only write), so a reader can open it where it is rather than
at the cover. Floored onto the spine-stats ruler, so it never sits past the
stored percent. Derived per read, never stored; `None` whenever
[`Self::epub_cfi`] is set or the book has no measured structure.

progress_percent.description:
Whole-book percent, 0..=100. `#[serde(default)]` — unlike its siblings
here — so a payload from a server predating this field still decodes.

oneOf.description:
Where this position actually is in the book. Read-path only, on the
same terms as [`Self::total_duration_seconds`].

total_duration_seconds.description:
Whole-book audio duration (sum of parts), so no caller has to source an
audiobook's runtime elsewhere to turn [`Self::audio_position_seconds`] into
a percent. `None` for epub rows. Read-path only: filled by
`GET /api/progress/{uuid}` and the resume feed, absent from the
`POST /api/progress` echo.

ProgressUpdate.description:
Progress-sync write payload. `format` discriminates which position
field is meaningful: `Epub` requires `epub_cfi`, `Audio` requires
`audio_position_seconds`. The server validates this at the handler
boundary via [`ProgressUpdate::validate`].

book_file_id.description:
The `book_files` row the position was taken in, for books carrying
more than one file of the format (two narrations of one audiobook).
`None` from a client that doesn't track it — the server then resolves
the same default file the manifest would have served.

client_updated_at.description:
Unix seconds when the client observed this position, used to resolve
most-recent-wins by **event** time rather than server receipt time. An older
client that never sends it still parses; `upsert_progress` then uses server
now.

kobo_location.description:
A Kobo's `CurrentBookmark.Location` object, serialized to a JSON
string and stored verbatim. Echoed back to the device for exact
resume; the server may additionally translate it to/from a CFI
(`db::kobo_position`), but no client ever renders it, and a string
keeps `shared` free of a `serde_json` runtime dependency.

progress_percent.description:
Whole-book percent, 0..=100. The cross-surface half of a position:
unlike a CFI or a `KoboSpan` it means the same thing everywhere. A
Kobo reports one and no CFI, so for `Epub` this satisfies the
"some position" requirement on its own.

ProviderCapabilities.description:
What one provider can be asked and what it can return, independent of
whether it is currently configured. A flag is a claim about the provider's
API, not one book: flip one only in the same change that teaches the
provider module to parse the field onto [`ProviderEdition`], because a
fixture cross-check fails a flag that outruns its parser.

ProviderEdition.description:
One candidate from one provider in a fan-out edition search, kept
**attributed and un-collapsed**: two editions sharing an ISBN across two
sources stay two entries, because telling editions apart is what the picker
is for. A separate type from [`ExternalBookMeta`], the frozen check-in wire
payload; convert with `TryFrom` where a check-in-shaped value is wanted.

first_publish_year.description:
Year the *work* was first published, across all editions — distinct
from `year`, which is this edition's own date.

genres.description:
Genres as this provider labels them, already sanitized and capped at
[`Self::MAX_GENRES`].

Empty means "this provider has none for this book"; whether a source can
answer for genres *at all* is [`ProviderCapabilities::carries_genres`].

isbn10.description:
ISBN-10 for the **same** printing as [`Self::isbn13`], when the provider
carries one. Only set when the two demonstrably name one edition, since
providers list identifiers per *work* as readily as per edition. `None` is
the normal answer for a 979-prefixed ISBN-13, which has no ISBN-10.

isbn13.description:
The normalized ISBN-13 (13 digits, no hyphens), when the provider ties one
to *this* edition. Optional on purpose: a search hit is often a *work*, not a
printing, so a candidate needs a [`Self::provider_ref`] to be re-fetched by,
not an ISBN. The check-in path still requires one (see [`ExternalBookMeta`]).

pages.description:
The edition's **printed** length, which is what the `print_pages`
override stores — never `books.page_count`, which is a comic's image
count. `None` when the provider doesn't say; a provider reporting `0`
for "unknown" is normalized to `None` rather than staged over a real
page count.

provider_ref.description:
Opaque, provider-scoped handle for re-fetching this candidate in full once
it is selected, since a thin search hit carries less than the provider's own
record. Omnibus never parses it: it is the provider's own id where one
exists, else `isbn:<isbn13>`, which every provider can be re-queried by.

relevance.description:
How strongly this candidate matches the query that found it, in
**hundredths of a point** (so `1000` is a perfect title match), or `None`
from a source that did not score. Derived from the candidate and the query
alone, never from which provider answered, so a source dropping out removes
its rows and reorders nothing.

series_index.description:
This book's position in [`Self::series`], formatted for display
(`"1"`, `"2.5"`), or `None` when the provider doesn't say.

Only Hardcover models a series position, so the *other* providers
always leave this `None` — the same asymmetry `series` itself has.

year.description: Publication year or date as the provider reports it (free text).

ProviderInfo.description:
One entry in the provider catalog, built by `providers::catalog` in
`omnibus-db` and served by `GET /api/metadata/providers`.

**Never carries key material** — `configured` is a bool, not a masked
preview, because this endpoint is reachable by any authenticated user.

configured.description:
Whether the ladder would actually invoke this provider right now —
always `true` for a keyless-capable provider, key-gated otherwise.
Mirrors the same check `providers::ladder` uses, so the two can never
disagree about what "configured" means.

requires_key.description:
Whether an API key is required to reach this provider at all (as
opposed to optional — present or not, the provider still answers).

ProviderSearchSource.description: One row of the per-source status table returned alongside the candidates.

oneOf.description:
The provider answered. `count` is how many of its candidates reached
the returned list — post-cap, so it never overstates what is there.
Not usable on this instance (no API key). No request was sent.

Asked, but no answer came back. `message` is the provider call's own
top-level context, never the error chain below it — which is where a
request URL, and so a `?key=`, would render.

Skipped without a request: this provider rate-limited us recently and is
still inside its cooldown.

Distinct from [`Self::Failed`]: nothing was asked, and `retry_after_secs`
says when it is worth asking again.

retry_after_secs.description: Whole seconds left on the cooldown, rounded up.

ProviderSearchStatus.description:
What one provider contributed to a fan-out search.

The three cases are the point of the type: "it has nothing", "we never
asked it", and "we asked and never got an answer" are different facts, and
collapsing them makes an outage read as a miss.

RankedEntity.description: A ranked entity (author or tag) by total active seconds in the window.

RatingBucket.description:
One bar of the star-rating distribution: a half-star bucket and how many
books the user rated into it within the window.

`half_stars` is the stored 1..=10 scale, **not** stars: renderers must halve
it (`stars()` does), or a 5-star rating reads as a 10-point scale.

RatingRecord.description:
Server-authoritative rating returned by the set/get endpoints. `updated_at`
is unix seconds (SQLite `strftime('%s')`).

stars.description: Star rating in `0.5..=5.0`, in half-star steps.

RatingUpdate.description: Write payload: set (or change) the current user's rating for a book.

stars.description: Star rating in `0.5..=5.0`, in half-star steps.

ReadStatus.description:
A book's read-lifecycle state for one user. Serializes as a plain lowercase
string (`"unread"` / `"reading"` / `"finished"`) matching the
`book_read_status.status` CHECK constraint.

ReadStatusRecord.description:
Server-authoritative read state returned by the set/get endpoints.
`updated_at` is unix seconds (SQLite `strftime('%s')`); `finished_at` is the
moment the book most recently became `finished` (`None` otherwise).

updated_at_iso.description:
[`Self::updated_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When the status last changed.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

ReadingGoal.description:
One reader's goal for one calendar year, paired with progress toward it.

`current` uses the **same completion definition as every other completion
metric on [`StatsSummary`]**, bounded to the goal's own year so raising this
year's target never moves last year's number.

current.description:
Progress toward `target` within `year`. May exceed it — a reader past
their goal is the good case, and clamping it here would hide it.

target.description:
The target the reader set. Always `>= 1`; a cleared goal is an absent
[`ReadingGoal`], never a zero target.

year.description:
The calendar year (reader's calendar) this goal and its `current`
count belong to.

ReadingGoalUpdate.description:
Write payload for `PUT /api/stats/goal`.

`year` and `kind` default to the server's current year and [`GOAL_KIND_BOOKS`],
so the common client sends `{"target": 24}` alone. A `null` / absent `target`
**clears** the goal for that `(year, kind)`; there is no separate DELETE route.

target.description:
Omitted rather than sent as `null` when clearing — the two decode
identically, and an omitted key keeps the wire honest about how little
the usual write carries.

RegisterRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/register`. See [`LoginRequest`] for
why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

RegistrationStatus.description:
Whether self-registration is open; the body of `GET /api/auth/registration`
and `POST /api/settings/registration`.

RenameApiTokenRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/auth/api-tokens/{id}` — the row's Rename action.

ResolveMetaRequest.description:
Resolve a picked title-search candidate against the library — the ladder's
library rungs applied to metadata already in hand, so no provider round
trip (which could miss on an ISBN the search itself just surfaced).

ResolvedPosition.description:
Where a stored position sits in the book, resolved server-side against the
spine/TOC data `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters` serves and the chapter marks
the player reads. Every field is optional because the structure may be
missing (a TOC-less EPUB, an audiobook with no marks); [`Self::confidence`]
says how much of the block to lean on.

chapter_ordinal.description:
1-based, so `chapter_ordinal` of [`Self::chapters_total`] reads
directly. Deliberately not the stored 0-based `ebook_chapters.ordinal`
— an off-by-one here is the whole failure this block exists to end.

percent_through_book.description:
0..=100 through the whole book, on the same ruler
`ProgressRecord::progress_percent` uses for epub rows.

spine_index.description:
0-based spine document index, matching `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters`.
`None` for audio positions and for a comic page anchor.

ResumePoint.description: "Pick up where you left off" entry returned by `GET /api/progress/recent` and `rpc_recent_progress`.

audio_part.description:
1-based structural part of the audiobook timeline at the saved position, from
the resolved file's marks. `None` for epub rows. **Not a book chapter:** the
marks are whatever the container carried (a 65-chapter novel stored as a
4-part M4B has four); book chapters live in [`ProgressRecord::resolved`].

audio_part_count.description: Total structural parts, for a "3 of 12" readout. `None` for epub rows.

oneOf.description:
For linked books: the mapped "resume in the other format" candidate
(absent when the other side is newer or unmappable).

linked.description:
Whether the user has confirmed a cross-format link for this book —
linked books collapse to one card carrying both resume affordances.

playback_rate.description:
The user's saved playback rate for this book, so resume surfaces can
rate-adjust their "left" readouts. `None` for epub rows and when no
preference has been saved (treat as 1x).

RuleField.description:
A field a smart rule can match on. Mirrors the advanced-search query vocabulary plus
the acquisition-date fields.

RuleOp.description: A comparison operator for a smart rule.

RulePreview.description: Live-preview result for the create modal: "N of M match" + sample covers.

RulePreviewRequest.description: Unsaved rule sent to the preview endpoint.

ScanBook.description:
A library book matched during scan resolution — just enough to display and
act on it (the confirm/decision screens).

has_files.description:
Whether the book has a digital file. `false` for a paper-only or
wishlist-only book, whose confirm screen must not claim the reader
"already has this one digitally". Defaulted so a payload from before
the field decodes; nothing before it emitted the flag.

has_physical.description: Whether the book already has ≥1 physical copy checked in.

isbn.description:
The book's own ISBN identifier, separator-stripped. Lets the close-match
confirm show the library edition's ISBN beside the scanned one.

oneOf.description: Exact identifier hit; the book already has a physical copy.

Exact identifier hit; on the caller's physical wishlist (no physical
copy yet). The book they wanted and now hold, so clients offer to check
the copy in, which clears the entry.
Exact identifier hit; in the library digitally, no physical copy yet.

Online-resolved and (title, author)-matched at least one library book:
needs a human "is this the book?" confirmation before any write. Carried as
head + tail so the single-candidate wire shape stays byte-identical for older
clients; clients that know both render `book` followed by `others` as one
picker.
Online-resolved but not in the library.
Neither the library nor any provider knew the ISBN.

ScanOutcome.description:
Outcome of resolving a scanned/typed ISBN down the matching ladder. A fuzzy
(title, author) hit is a [`ScanOutcome::CloseMatch`] — never auto-resolved;
the client must confirm before any write, so a hit on several rows is a
picker rather than a reason to decline the match.

ScanSearchRequest.description:
Search the external providers by title text — the fallback offered when an
ISBN scan resolves to [`ScanOutcome::Unresolved`].

ScanSearchResponse.description:
Title-search results: provider-resolved candidates for the reader to pick
from, each complete enough to feed [`ResolveMetaRequest`].

SeriesDetail.description:
Series detail payload for `GET /api/series/:id` and `rpc_get_series`.
Books are ordered by `series_index`.

SeriesStack.description: A series folded into one grid tile.

lead_uuid.description: The member standing in the result list; the stack renders in its slot.

members.description: Every member in the result set, in series order.

series_id.description: The series page to link, when one resolves.

states.description: One state per member on server pages; empty on client-grouped stacks.

SeriesSummary.description:
Lightweight series row for the `/series` index. Carries the primary
author of the series (first book's first creator) so the card can
render the by-line without a second fetch.

accent.description: Accent color borrowed from the first book in the series with one.

primary_author.description:
Primary author display string (first book's first creator). `None`
when the series has no books with a linked author.

SessionFormat.description:
Which of the two session tables a stitched sitting drew from.

[`Self::Mixed`] is not a fallback: a dual-format book read and listened to in
one stretch stitches into a single sitting (see `db::stats::sessionize`), and
naming either format alone would misreport it.

SessionLogEntry.description:
One sitting in the reading-session log: adjacent checkpoint rows stitched
back together, so an entry is a sit rather than a heartbeat flush.

`seconds` is the *recorded* time, not `ended_at - started_at`: a paused
sitting spans more wall clock than it recorded.

ended_at.description: Unix seconds of its last checkpoint row's end.

ended_at_iso.description:
[`Self::ended_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When it ended.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

started_at.description: Unix seconds of the sitting's first checkpoint row.

started_at_iso.description:
[`Self::started_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When the sitting began.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

SessionLogPage.description: One page of the reading-session log, newest first.

next_before.description:
The cursor for the next page, or `None` at the end of the log. Encoded
rather than structured so a client pages by echoing it back without
knowing how the keyset is built.

SessionReport.description:
Batched session row (reader / audio open-to-close span). Mobile
posts these on reconnect via `POST /api/progress/sessions`; web posts
best-effort on unmount. `progress_units` is seconds_read (epub) or
seconds_listened (audio).

client_id.description:
Handle minted by the device that recorded the session, making a
replay idempotent (migration 0052). A queued report is retried
whenever the reply was lost rather than the request, and without a
handle each retry appended a second row. `None` for web clients,
which post once and never retry.

time_zone.description:
IANA zone name on the recording device at capture time
(`"America/Los_Angeles"`, `"Asia/Tokyo"`), recorded **alongside**
[`Self::utc_offset_minutes`]: the offset says what the clock read, the zone
says *where* (`-420` is Los Angeles in summer, Phoenix year-round). `None`
from a client that doesn't report one and on older rows.

utc_offset_minutes.description:
Minutes east of UTC on the recording device at capture time (`-420` for
UTC-7, `330` for UTC+05:30). The time-of-day rollups bucket `started_at`
against this instead of UTC (see `db::stats::patterns`). `None` from a client
that doesn't report one and on older rows, which the time-pattern charts
exclude rather than default to UTC.

SessionView.description:
A session row as shown to its owner or an admin (device & session
management). Never exposes the token hash — only enough to
identify and revoke the row. Shared by the self-service
`GET /api/auth/sessions` and the admin `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/sessions`.

client.description:
Human-readable name of the client holding this session — the registered
device's name for a native client ("Seamus's iPhone"), otherwise a label
derived from the captured `User-Agent` ("Firefox on macOS"). Derived
server-side so the raw header never reaches a page; falls back to
[`UNKNOWN_CLIENT`] for a session minted before migration `0088`.

is_current.description:
`true` when this is the session the request authenticated with. Only set by
the self-service listing; the admin listing always returns `false`, even for
the admin's own session. Enforcement lives on the write side: the self-service
`DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` refuses (400) to revoke the request's own
session id.

recorded.description:
How many sessions named a book the server knows; it drops the rest, so this can be
less than the number sent. A session repeating a stored `client_id` counts here but
isn't stored twice.

SetBookDetailScrollStops.description: Whether a book's detail page stops at each section as you scroll.

enabled.description: `true` stops at each section; `false` scrolls the page in one piece.

key.description:
The Google Books API key, up to 512 bytes. `null`, absent or blank clears the
saved key.

The Hardcover API token, up to 2048 bytes. `null`, absent or blank clears the
saved key.

SetHiddenFormats.description: The formats to hide from your library view.

formats.description:
Format names such as `cbz`, each 1 to 16 letters or digits, at most 32. Case and
duplicates don't matter. An empty or missing list hides nothing.

email.description:
The address books are emailed to, such as `name@kindle.com`. Null, missing or
blank clears it.

SetPasswordRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/users/{id}/password` (admin password
reset). See [`LoginRequest`] for why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

display_name.description:
The name other readers see, up to 64 characters with no control characters.
Null, missing or blank clears it, and your username shows instead.

SetReadStatus.description: Write payload: set the current user's read state for a book.

SetShareStats.description: Whether other readers on this server can see your reading stats.

enabled.description: `true` shares your stats with the household; `false` keeps them to yourself.

SetStackSeries.description: Whether your library grid shows each series as one tile.

enabled.description: `true` folds a series into one tile; `false` shows every book on its own.

Settings.description:
User-configurable paths for the ebook and audiobook libraries, plus the
optional periodic-rescan cadence.

scan_interval_hours.description:
Hours between automatic rescans of both libraries. `None` disables periodic
scanning: the library then only reindexes on server boot or a manual "Scan
Library" click. Omitted from the wire payload when unset, so existing callers
see no change to the `Settings` JSON shape.

Shelf.description: Full shelf detail: the summary fields plus description, rule, and match mode.

oneOf.description: `Some` for smart shelves, `None` for manual.

owner_has_avatar.description:
Whether the owner has uploaded an avatar — see
[`ShelfSummary::owner_has_avatar`].

owner_username.description: Owner's username, for `by <name>` attribution on shelves you don't own.

sync_to_kobo.description:
Whether this shelf's books are exposed to the owner's Kobo devices over
wireless sync. Off by default — sync is never whole-library.

ShelfKind.description: Kind of shelf, fixed at creation.

ShelfPage.description: One page of a shelf's books (v1: capped, no cursor).

ShelfSummary.description: Compact shelf row for the rail: identity, kind, visibility, accent, count.

cover_uuids.description:
Up to four member book uuids (cover-bearing members first, shelf
default order) for gallery mosaic tiles. `default` keeps payloads from
older servers deserializable.

owner_has_avatar.description:
Whether the owner has uploaded an avatar, so attribution can draw
`GET /api/users/{owner_user_id}/avatar` instead of a monogram.
`default` keeps payloads from older servers deserializable.

owner_username.description: Owner's username, for `by <name>` attribution on shelves you don't own.

SmtpConfigStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide SMTP config for the Settings UI. **Never
carries the raw password** — only a short masked preview.

password_masked.description: Short masked preview of the password (e.g. `pa…rd`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective config comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

SmtpConfigUpdate.description:
Admin request to save (or partially update) the server-wide SMTP config.

Deliberately does not derive `Debug`: it carries a plaintext SMTP password
that a stray `tracing::debug!(?req)` would log. `password` is `None` to leave
the stored password unchanged; a `Some("")` clears it.

SmtpSecurity.description: Transport security for the outbound SMTP connection.

SortDir.description: Ascending or descending sort direction for a [`SortKey`].

SortKey.description: Sortable axes exposed in the toolbar / table headers.

SpoilerFilter.description:
What to do about hits that sit past the reader's own position.

The default annotates rather than excludes, so an agent can say "there's an
answer, but it's ahead of you"; `Exclude` is for callers who must not see the
payoff at all.

StackMemberState.description: The viewer's reading state for one member of a stack.

percent.description: Whole-book percent (0-100) from the ebook position, if any.

started.description: Opened in any format: a status, a percent, or a listening position.

StatsRange.description:
Reporting window for the stats page. Serializes as a compact snake-case
string so the wire shape stays stable across the RPC boundary.

StatsSummary.description:
The full aggregate payload for one user over one [`StatsRange`].

A book counts as finished from a 100% `journal_entries` row or a `finished`
`book_read_status` (once if both, live books only); every completion metric
shares that definition. `pages_read` measures ground covered instead.

as_of_day.description:
Today on the reader's calendar (`YYYY-MM-DD`) when the summary was
computed. Anchors the heatmap's trailing-year grid so the client
never bakes its own clock into render (rule 07).

avg_stars.description:
Mean of the user's star ratings (0.5..=5.0) over books rated within
the window; `None` when nothing was rated. `f64` keeps the struct
`PartialEq`-only.

books_active.description: Distinct books with any session activity in the window.

books_per_month.description:
Books finished per month over the trailing 12 calendar months, oldest
first, ending at the current (possibly partial) month. Independent of
`range` — the all-time section's trend chart is never tied to the
period switcher.

books_this_year.description:
Books finished in the current calendar year, whether or not an annual goal
is set: the figure a surface can show *before* a reader commits to a target.
It is the same measurement [`ReadingGoal::current`] carries, computed once, so
setting a goal never appears to move the count. Not windowed, like
[`Self::goal`]: it reads the same on every [`StatsRange`].

busiest_week_start.description:
Monday (`YYYY-MM-DD`, reader's calendar) of the busiest ISO week, if any
— the week's own start, so a surface can label it "Week of …" whether or
not the reader happened to read on the Monday.

current_streak_days.description:
Consecutive active days still running as of [`Self::as_of_day`]: the streak
the reader is *on*, where `longest_streak_days` is the record. A run ending
yesterday still counts; one ending earlier reports zero. **Not windowed**,
unlike every other figure here: it is a fact about right now, so it reads the
same on every `StatsRange`.

daily_goals.description:
The caller's standing daily goals and today's progress toward them.
Not windowed either, and for the same reason as `goal`: a daily target
recurs, so it reads the same whichever [`StatsRange`] the page shows.

day_of_week.description:
Active seconds in the window by local weekday — all 7 buckets, Monday
first, zeros included. Same scoping and same exclusion as
[`Self::hour_of_day`], so the two strips always describe one set of
sessions and sum to the same total.

genre_tagged_books.description:
Distinct books with a genre *and* activity in the window — the
population `genre_share`'s slices are drawn from, and the donut's
center count. Always `<= books_active`; the difference is reading the
ring cannot describe, which the card discloses rather than absorbing
into a total that would overstate what the slices cover.

oneOf.description:
The caller's goal for the **current calendar year**, `None` when none
is set. Like `current_streak_days` this is deliberately *not* windowed:
a goal is annual by definition, so it reads the same on every
[`StatsRange`] and a period switch never moves it.

hour_of_day.description:
Active seconds in the window by **local** hour of day: all 24 buckets,
ascending, zeros included. Reading and listening together. Bucketed
server-side against each session's capture-time UTC offset; sessions with no
recorded offset are **not** in these totals and are reported separately as
[`Self::unzoned_seconds`].

length_buckets.description:
Books finished in the window bucketed by length, plus the unknown
bucket. Every bucket is present, zeros included; an all-zero set means
nothing was finished, which the surfaces render as an empty state
rather than flat bars.

listening_daily.description:
Daily listening seconds within `range`'s window — the Listening
tile's drill-in trend chart.

pages_detail.description:
What `pages_read` could and could not see in this window, plus the day
the ledger behind it started. Server-owned so the web tile and the iOS
tile cannot disagree about which empty state a window is in.

pages_per_hour.description:
Estimated reading speed over the window, in pages per hour: a
**seconds-weighted** mean over books *finished* in the window that resolve a
length (above zero pages) and carry recorded reading time. Not `pages_read`
over `reading_seconds`, which cover different books. Reading time only, so a
book read partly in audio over-reports. `None` when no finished book qualifies.

pages_read.description:
Pages read in the window (the Pages tile): the ground each book was carried
over inside the window, from the forward-progress ledger, against its length
on the one ladder in `db::stats::pages`. Exact for some books, an estimate
for others. `None` when no book read resolves a length (an unmeasured book
adds nothing, not zero); see [`Self::pages_detail`] before rendering "no data".

previous.description:
The immediately preceding window's aggregates, for the drill-in's
vs-previous-period delta.

rating_histogram.description:
How the window's ratings are distributed across the ten half-star
buckets — the shape `avg_stars` flattens into one number. All ten
buckets are present, zeros included; an empty vec means the window
carries no ratings at all. Scoped exactly as `avg_stars` is, so the
bucket counts sum to the set the mean is taken over.

rating_monthly.description:
Mean star rating per month over the trailing 12 calendar months —
the Avg rating tile's drill-in trend chart. Independent of `range`,
same trailing-window convention as `books_per_month`. A month with
nothing rated carries `0.0`, which no real mean (at least half a star)
can, so renderers draw it as empty rather than as a low rating.

sessions.description:
Sittings in the window — checkpoint rows stitched back together per
book, glances excluded. Not a row count: see [`BookInsights::sessions`].

superlatives.description:
The window's single most-X figures. Scoped to `range` like the rest of
this struct. [`Superlatives::is_empty`] is a predicate over these five,
**not** the card's render gate — the surfaces draw rows off fields
outside this struct too, so gating on it would drop a card that still
has something to show. See that method's docs.

unzoned_seconds.description:
Active seconds in the window that carry no capture-time UTC offset and so
can't be placed on a local clock (older rows, or a client that doesn't report
one). Surfaced rather than folded into UTC or some later offset, which would
invent where the reader was. A non-zero value discloses that the two strips
cover less than the window's total; it is not an error.

StorageStats.description: Disk usage across the book library and every on-disk cache.

library_bytes.description:
Sum of `book_files.size_bytes` — the on-disk footprint of the
indexed library itself (not a cache, so it carries no cap).

oneOf.description: No Hardcover key is configured — the UI shows a connect message.
A resolution is enqueued and nothing is cached yet — the UI polls.

Cached results. `items` may be empty (sticky negative — Hardcover
matched nothing usable).

SuggestionsResponse.description: Response for a book's suggestions strip.

SummarySource.description: Which external provider a summary fetch should hit.

Superlatives.description:
The window's single most-X figures — the ranked one-liners a total can't
say, and the shape a recap leads with.

**Every field is optional, and an absent one is the point.** A window that
can't support a superlative omits it rather than crowning its only datum.

oneOf.description:
The single day with the most active seconds in the window, reading and
listening together. Ties break to the earliest day.

The book finished in the window in the fewest **days** from its first
recorded session (a same-day read counts as one). Only books with at least
[`FASTEST_READ_MIN_SECS`] of recorded time are eligible, and this is a **lower
bound** on the real time, since untracked reading is invisible here.
Surfaces must say so.

The longest book finished in the window, in **pages** as resolved by
the shared length ladder (`db::stats::pages`). Absent when nothing
finished in the window resolves a length.

The longest single sitting in the window, in **seconds** — stitched
checkpoint rows, so this is how long the reader actually sat, not how
long a client waited between flushes.

The shortest book finished in the window, in **pages**. Absent when
it would name the same book as `longest_book`, or carry the same page
count — a pair that reads as a range when there isn't one.

TagWeight.description: Single tag with its book count, for the tag cloud.

TaskKind.description:
Discriminant for [`TaskProgress`] entries. Mirrors the payload-less
shape of the server-side `Task` enum so the wire protocol stays
decoupled from the runtime `Task` type's lifetimes and handler
closures. `#[non_exhaustive]` so future worker actions can be added
without breaking client matches.

TrendPoint.description:
One point in a metric's drill-in trend chart: a period label (a day
`YYYY-MM-DD` or a month `YYYY-MM`, depending on the series) and the
metric's value over that period.

UndoMergeRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/books/merge/undo`: the `merge_log` id to reverse.

UndoMergeResult.description: Result of a successful unmerge: the restored (source) book's uuid.

UpdateBookmark.description: Payload for updating a bookmark's title/note. `None` clears the title.

UpdateCopyNoteRequest.description:
Body of the copy-note edit (`PATCH /api/physical/copies/{id}`). `None` — and
any blank string — clears the note.

UpdateHighlightNote.description: Payload for updating a highlight's note text.

UpdateJournalEntry.description:
Write payload: edit an existing journal entry's body and/or progress.
`status: Some(_)` transitions the entry (publish a draft); `None` — the
default, so pre-drafts clients are unaffected — keeps the stored status.

UpdateShelfRequest.description:
Partial update. `None` fields are left unchanged. `rules` replaces the whole
rule set (smart shelves only).

sync_to_kobo.description: Toggle the shelf's Kobo wireless-sync opt-in.

UploadCommitResult.description:
Result of a successful commit: the durable uuid of the newly-filed book,
so the client can navigate straight to its detail page.

UploadInspection.description:
Auto-extracted metadata returned by the inspect step, mirroring what the
indexer would read from the file's embedded metadata. The reader can correct
any field before committing; the corrected `title`/`author` drive the
on-disk folder. The original four fields stay top-level and the rest are
`#[serde(default)]`, so an older server's reply still decodes.

author.description: The first creator the file declares — what the Author field holds.

cover_preview.description:
A small `data:` URL of the file's cover, so the review form can show it
before the book exists and there is a cover route to point at. `None`
when the file has no cover or it could not be decoded.

creators.description:
Every creator the file declares, in file order, `author` first. The
review form shows the rest so it never under-reports what the commit
will save. Defaulted so an older server's reply still decodes.

ext.description: Lowercased file extension the server settled on (e.g. `"epub"`).

has_cover.description: Whether the file carried an embedded (or sidecar) cover.

identifiers.description: Every typed identifier the file declares, for the sidebar.

isbn13.description: The ISBN-13 the indexer would derive from the file's identifiers.

subjects.description: The file's `<dc:subject>` entries — the review form's Tags.

UserPermissions.description:
The four permission booleans that define what a user can do. `is_admin`
is presented in the UI as an "Administrator" permission that implies the
other three; the storage layer keeps them as independent flags (there is
no role enum). Used by the admin create/edit endpoints.

UserSummary.description: Safe projection of a `users` row. No password fields ever cross the wire.

book_detail_scroll_stops.description:
Whether this user's book detail page uses the snap-stop marquee.
`false` — the default, and what a pre-0092 payload decodes to —
renders it as one continuous scroll.

display_name.description:
Presentation name other users see, or `None` to fall back to
[`Self::username`] — which stays the login and admin identity.

has_avatar.description:
Whether this user has uploaded an avatar. Clients render
`GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` when set and a monogram otherwise.

hidden_formats.description:
Formats this user hides from the landing All Books view — canonical
lowercase tokens (`"cbz"`). Clients pass it back as the listing
request's `exclude_formats`; empty means nothing hidden.

kindle_email.description:
Send-to-Kindle destination address, or `None` when the user hasn't
configured one. Non-secret — the user set it themselves.

share_stats.description:
Whether other readers on this server may see this user's stats page.
`true` — the default, and what a pre-0099 payload decodes to.

stack_series.description: Whether this user's landing grid folds each series into one tile.

Visibility.description: Who can see a shelf. `Private` = owner + admins; `Public` = every user.

WeekdayBucket.description:
One column of the day-of-week strip: a weekday in the reader's local
calendar and the active seconds recorded on it. `weekday` is 0 = Monday ..
6 = Sunday, and the server sends `label` with it because week-start is a
convention a client could get wrong. [`StatsSummary::day_of_week`] always
carries all 7, Monday first, zeros included.

WishlistAddRequest.description:
Add a book to the caller's physical wishlist — either an existing library
book (`book_uuid`) or a new fileless book from external meta. Set one; if
both are present `book_uuid` wins and `meta` is ignored.

WishlistEntry.description: A book on one user's physical wishlist. Unique per `(user_id, book_uuid)`.

WishlistRemoval.description:
What removing a wishlist entry did beyond dropping the row. A book that
existed only to be wanted — no file, no copy, nobody else's wish — goes
with its last entry, and `book_deleted` is how the client learns the page
it is standing on is gone.

WishlistSource.description:
Where a wishlist entry was added from. Persisted as the `source` column.

The check-in flow has three front doors a reader tells apart: a barcode read
off the cover, an ISBN typed at the keypad, and a title search whose ISBN
came from the *provider* rather than the reader.

WorkerQueueEntry.description:
One [`TaskKind`]'s live queue depth and recent completion timings.
Timings are milliseconds (wire-friendly; the db-side `Worker::metrics`
uses `std::time::Duration`, which doesn't serialize), oldest first.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/auth/login`, or an API token (`omni_…`) from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`.

media_token.name: token
media_token.description: A bearer token passed in the URL, for media that an `` or `

session_cookie.name: __Host-omnibus_session
session_cookie.description: The cookie a browser sign-in sets. A server running without secure cookies (`OMNIBUS_SECURE_COOKIES=0`) names it `omnibus_session` instead.
